title.zh: 卷十二 隋本紀下第十二: 煬帝 恭帝
title.en: Volume 12 Sui Annals 2: Emperor Yang, Emperor Gong
title.raw: 卷十二 隋本紀下第十二: 煬帝 恭帝 Volume 12 Sui Annals 2: Emperor Yang, Emperor Gong

sentences.zh: 煬帝 恭帝

translations.literal: Emperor Yang; Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang and Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 煬皇帝諱廣，一名英，小字阿𡡉，高祖第二子也。

translations.literal: The Emperor Yang, taboo name Guang, also named Ying, childhood name A-mo, was the second son of Emperor Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang, taboo name Guang, also called Ying, childhood name A-mo, was Gaozu's second son.

sentences.zh: 母曰文獻獨孤皇后。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress Wenxian of the Dugu clan.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Wenxian, née Dugu.

sentences.zh: 上美姿儀，少敏慧。

translations.literal: The Emperor was handsome in bearing and quick-witted from youth.
translations.idiomatic: He was striking in appearance and clever even as a boy.

sentences.zh: 高祖及後於諸子中，特所鐘愛。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu and the empress especially favored him among all their sons.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and the empress singled him out for special affection among the princes.

sentences.zh: 在周以高祖勛，封雁門郡公。

translations.literal: In Zhou, on account of Gaozu's merit, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yanmen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhou period, thanks to Gaozu's achievements, he received the title Duke of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 開皇元年，立為晉王，拜柱國、并州總管，時年十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he was installed as Prince of Jin, appointed Pillar of State and Area Commander of Bing Province, aged thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year one he became Prince of Jin, Pillar of State, and commander of Bing Province at thirteen.

sentences.zh: 尋授武衛大將軍，進上柱國、河北道行臺尚書令，大將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made Grand General of the Martial Guard, advanced to Supreme Pillar of State and Acting Area Commander-in-Chief of the Hebei Circuit, retaining his rank as grand general.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named Grand General of the Martial Guard, then Supreme Pillar of State and acting Hebei circuit commander, keeping his grand general rank.

sentences.zh: 高祖令項城公歆、安道公李徹輔導之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered Duke of Xiangcheng Xin and Duke of Andao Li Che to guide and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu appointed Duke Xin of Xiangcheng and Duke Li Che of Andao as his tutors.

sentences.zh: 上好學，善屬文，沈深嚴重，朝野屬望。

translations.literal: The Emperor loved learning, was skilled at literary composition, grave and weighty in manner, and the court and common people looked to him with hope.
translations.idiomatic: He studied eagerly, wrote well, and carried himself with solemn gravity; court and country alike pinned their hopes on him.

sentences.zh: 高祖密令善相者來和遍視諸子。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu secretly ordered the skilled physiognomist Lai He to examine all his sons in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu secretly sent the physiognomist Lai He to read each prince in turn.

sentences.zh: 和曰：「晉王眉上雙骨隆起，貴不可言。

translations.literal: Lai said: "Above the Prince of Jin's brows the twin bones rise—his nobility is beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: Lai said, "The Prince of Jin's brows show twin ridges rising—his rank is beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 」既而高祖幸上所居第，見樂器弦多斷絕，又有塵埃，若不用者，以為不好聲妓之玩。

translations.literal: " Later Gaozu visited the Emperor's residence and saw that many instrument strings were broken and covered with dust, as if unused, and took this to mean he did not care for music and entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: " When Gaozu later visited his quarters, he found lutes with broken strings and dust on them, as though untouched, and concluded the prince scorned music and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 上尤自矯飾，當時稱為仁孝。

translations.literal: The Emperor especially cultivated an outward show of restraint, and at the time he was praised as benevolent and filial.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated an air of restraint all the more, and men of the day called him benevolent and filial.

sentences.zh: 嘗觀獵遇雨，左右進油衣，上曰：「士卒皆沾濕，我獨衣此乎！

translations.literal: Once on a hunt he met rain, and when attendants offered him an oiled cloak he said: "The soldiers are all soaked—shall I alone wear this?
translations.idiomatic: Once, hunting in rain, his attendants brought an oiled cloak; he said, "The troops are drenched—shall I alone stay dry?

sentences.zh: 」乃令持去。

translations.literal: " He then ordered it taken away.
translations.idiomatic: He then had it carried off.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉淮南道行臺尚書令。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Acting Area Commander-in-Chief of the Huainan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he became acting Huainan circuit commander.

sentences.zh: 其年，徵拜雍州牧、內史令。

translations.literal: That year he was summoned and appointed Governor of Yong Province and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was recalled as Governor of Yong and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 八年冬，大舉伐陳，以上為行軍元帥。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighth year a great campaign was launched against Chen, with the Emperor as supreme commander of the army.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of year eight the great assault on Chen began, with him as campaign commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，執陳湘州刺史施文慶、散騎常侍沈客卿、市令湯慧朗、刑法監徐析、尚書都令史暨慧，以其邪佞，有害於民，斬之石闕下以謝三吳。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he seized Chen's Inspector of Xiangzhou Shi Wenqing, Regular Attendant Shen Keqing, Market Chief Tang Huilang, Supervisor of Punishments Xu Qi, and Chief Clerk of the Secretariat Ji Hui, and because their wicked flattery had harmed the people, beheaded them below the Stone Gate to answer to the Three Wu.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen's fall he took Shi Wenqing, inspector of Xiangzhou, Shen Keqing, regular attendant, Tang Huilang, market chief, Xu Qi, punishment supervisor, and Ji Hui, secretariat chief clerk, and because their treachery had harmed the people, executed them beneath the Stone Gate as amends to the Three Wu.

sentences.zh: 於是封府庫資財，無所取，天下稱賢。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sealed the treasuries and took nothing from their wealth, and the realm called him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the storehouses and touched none of the loot, and the empire praised his virtue.

sentences.zh: 進位太尉，賜路車、乘馬、袞冕之服，玄圭、白璧各一雙。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Commandant and granted a state chariot, riding horses, and the robes of investiture, together with one pair each of the black jade tablet and white jade disc.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Commandant and given a state carriage, horses, investiture robes, and paired black and white jade emblems.

sentences.zh: 復拜并州總管。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Area Commander of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made commander of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 俄而江南高智慧等相聚作亂，徙上為揚州總管，鎮江都，每歲一朝。

translations.literal: Before long Gao Zhihui and others south of the Yangtze gathered in rebellion; the Emperor was moved to Area Commander of Yang Province and stationed at Jiangdu, attending court once each year.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gao Zhihui and other rebels rose south of the river; he was shifted to Yangzhou commander and posted at Jiangdu, coming to court once a year.

sentences.zh: 高祖之祠太山也，領武候大將軍。

translations.literal: When Gaozu sacrificed at Mount Tai, he led the Martial Guard grand general.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu worshipped at Mount Tai, he commanded the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 明年，歸籓，後數載，突厥寇邊，復為行軍元帥，出靈武。

translations.literal: The next year he returned to his fief; several years later, when the Turks raided the border, he was again made campaign commander-in-chief and marched out from Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he went back to his domain; years later, when Turks struck the frontier, he again led the army out from Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 無虜而旋。

translations.literal: He returned without encountering the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He came back without meeting the foe.

sentences.zh: 及太子勇廢，立上為皇太子。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Yong was deposed, the Emperor was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Yong was removed, he was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 是月，當受冊。

translations.literal: That month he was to receive the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: That month he was due to be enfeoffed as heir.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「吾以大興公成帝業。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "I achieved the imperial enterprise as Duke of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "I won the throne as Duke of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 」令上出舍大興。

translations.literal: " He ordered the prince to leave the palace and lodge at Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the prince to quit the palace and stay at Daxing.

sentences.zh: 其夜，烈風大雪，地震山崩，民舍多壞，壓死者百餘口。

translations.literal: That night fierce wind and heavy snow struck, the earth quaked and mountains collapsed, many houses were ruined, and more than a hundred people were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: That night a gale and blizzard rose, the ground shook and hills fell, houses collapsed by the score, and over a hundred people were buried alive.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，奉詔巡撫東南。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was ordered by edict to tour and inspect the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Renshou era he was commanded to tour the southeast.

sentences.zh: 是後，高祖每避署仁壽宮，恒令上監國。

translations.literal: After this, whenever Gaozu withdrew to the Renshou Palace for the summer, he always left the Emperor to oversee the state.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever Gaozu summered at Renshou Palace, he left the prince to govern.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，高祖崩，上即皇帝位於仁壽宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year Gaozu died, and the Emperor took the throne at Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year four Gaozu died, and the prince ascended at Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 八月，奉梓宮還京師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he escorted the coffin back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he brought the coffin home to the capital.

sentences.zh: 并州總管、漢王諒舉兵反，詔尚書左僕射楊素討平之。

translations.literal: The Area Commander of Bing Province, Prince of Han Liang, raised troops in rebellion; an edict ordered Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Yang Su to suppress and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang of Han, commander of Bing, rebelled; the edict sent Left Vice Director Yang Su to crush him.

sentences.zh: 九月乙巳，以備身將軍崔彭為左領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: On the day yisi of the ninth month, Palace Guard General Cui Peng was appointed Left Commander-in-Chief of the Leading Army.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi of the ninth month, Palace Guard General Cui Peng became Left Commander of the Leading Army.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙未，幸洛陽。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei of the eleventh month he visited Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei of the eleventh month he went to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 丙申，發丁男十數萬掘塹，自龍門東接長平、汲郡，抵臨清關，度河，至浚儀，襄城，達於上洛，以置關防。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen he drafted tens of thousands of laborers to dig trenches from Longmen east through Changping and Ji Commandery to Linqing Pass, crossed the river to Junyi and Xiangcheng, and reached Shangluo, to set up frontier defenses.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen he levied tens of thousands of men to dig trenches from Longmen east through Changping and Ji to Linqing Pass, across the river through Junyi and Xiangcheng to Shangluo, establishing border defenses.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，詔曰：幹道變化，陰陽所以消息；

translations.literal: On the day guichou an edict said: The transformations of the Way of Heaven are how yin and yang send forth their messages;
translations.idiomatic: On guichou an edict read: Heaven's Way shifts, and yin and yang thereby exchange their signs;

sentences.zh: 沿創不同，生靈所以順序。

translations.literal: successive creations differ, and thereby living beings keep their order.
translations.idiomatic: each creation differs, and living things thereby keep their place.

sentences.zh: 若使天意不變，施化何以成四時？

translations.literal: If Heaven's intent never changed, how could transformation bring forth the four seasons?
translations.idiomatic: Were Heaven's mind never to change, how could change fashion the four seasons?

sentences.zh: 人事不易，為政何以利萬姓？

translations.literal: If human affairs never changed, how could government benefit the myriad people?
translations.idiomatic: Were human affairs never to shift, how could rule profit the myriad folk?

sentences.zh: 《易》不雲乎，通其變，使民不倦。

translations.literal: Does not the Changes say: penetrate change and the people do not weary.
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "Comprehend change and the people will not tire.

sentences.zh: 變則通，通則久。

translations.literal: Change brings penetration; penetration brings endurance.
translations.idiomatic: Change yields penetration; penetration yields endurance.

sentences.zh: 有德則可久，有功則可大。

translations.literal: Where there is virtue there can be endurance; where there is achievement there can be greatness.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue endures; merit grows great.

sentences.zh: 朕又聞之，安安而能遷，民用丕變。

translations.literal: I have also heard that secure in security yet able to move—thus the people undergo great change.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard too that dwelling in peace yet able to migrate—the people thereby transform deeply.

sentences.zh: 是故姬邑兩周，如武王之意；

translations.literal: Therefore the Zhou capital had two Zhou cities, as King Wu intended;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Zhou had twin capitals at Zhou, as King Wu wished;

sentences.zh: 殷人五徙，成湯後之業。

translations.literal: the Yin people moved five times, completing the enterprise after Cheng Tang.
translations.idiomatic: the Yin moved five times, fulfilling the work begun after Cheng Tang.

sentences.zh: 若不因民順天，功業見乎變，愛民治國者，可不謂歟。

translations.literal: If one does not follow the people and accord with Heaven, how can achievement appear through change? Can one who loves the people and governs the state fail to act thus?
translations.idiomatic: Without following the people and obeying Heaven, how is achievement shown in change? Who governs with love for the people and does not do likewise?

sentences.zh: 然雒邑自古之都，王畿之內，天地之所合，陰陽之所和；

translations.literal: Yet Luoyang has been the ancient capital, within the royal domain where Heaven and Earth unite and yin and yang harmonize;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Luoyang is the ancient capital, within the royal domain where Heaven and Earth meet and yin and yang join;

sentences.zh: 控以三河，固以四塞；

translations.literal: gripped by the Three Rivers, secured by the Four Passes;
translations.idiomatic: held by the Three Rivers, barred by the Four Passes;

sentences.zh: 水陸通，貢賦等。

translations.literal: water and land routes connect, and tribute and levies arrive alike.
translations.idiomatic: with water and land routes open and tribute flowing equal from all quarters.

sentences.zh: 故漢祖曰：「吾行天下多矣，唯見雒陽。

translations.literal: Thus the Han Founder said: "I have traveled all under Heaven much, and only Luoyang have I seen.
translations.idiomatic: So the Han founder said, "I have ranged the empire wide, and only Luoyang have I seen.

sentences.zh: 」自古皇王，何嘗不留意，所不都者，蓋有由焉。

translations.literal: " From antiquity, which emperor-king has not taken note? That they did not make it their capital surely had its reasons.
translations.idiomatic: " Which sage king since antiquity has not noticed it? That they did not establish the throne there surely had cause.

sentences.zh: 或以九州未一，或以困其府庫，作雒之制，所以未暇也。

translations.literal: Some because the Nine Provinces were not yet one, some because their treasuries were strained—the design for Luoyang therefore had no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Some because the nine provinces were not yet united, some because the treasury was strained—building Luoyang therefore went untended.

sentences.zh: 我有隋之始，便欲創茲懷、雒，日復一日，越暨於今。

translations.literal: From the beginning of our Sui I wished to found this design at Huai and Luo, day after day, until it reaches the present.
translations.idiomatic: From the founding of Sui I have wished to raise this plan at Huai and Luo, day upon day, until now.

sentences.zh: 念茲在茲，興言感哽。

translations.literal: Thinking of it, dwelling on it, I speak and am moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: It fills my thoughts; when I speak of it, grief catches my throat.

sentences.zh: 朕肅膺寶歷，纂臨萬邦，遵而不失，心奉先誌。

translations.literal: I reverently received the precious succession and now rule the myriad states, following without lapse and in my heart serving the former aim.
translations.idiomatic: I reverently took the sacred succession and govern ten thousand realms, holding fast without fail to my predecessor's intent.

sentences.zh: 今者，漢王諒悖逆，毒被山東；

translations.literal: Now Prince of Han Liang has rebelled in treachery, and his poison has spread through Shandong;
translations.idiomatic: Now Prince Liang of Han has turned traitor, and his poison has spread across Shandong;

sentences.zh: 遂令州縣，或淪非所。

translations.literal: thereby causing prefectures and counties to fall outside their proper allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: so that prefectures and counties have fallen to the wrong side.

sentences.zh: 由關河懸遠，兵不赴急。

translations.literal: Because the passes and rivers lie far apart, troops could not hurry to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: Because passes and rivers stand remote, armies could not reach the emergency in time.

sentences.zh: 加以并州移戶，復在河南；

translations.literal: Moreover households from Bing Province were moved, again settling south of the river;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover households of Bing were relocated, again to settle south of the river;

sentences.zh: 周遷殷民，意在於此。

translations.literal: when Zhou moved the Yin people, the intent lay here.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhou moved the Yin people, the purpose was the same.

sentences.zh: 況復南服遐遠，東夏殷大，因機順動，今也其時。

translations.literal: How much more when the southern domains are far, and the eastern summer is vast—seizing the moment and following the movement, now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: All the more when the south is distant and the eastern lands are vast—to move with the moment and follow the tide, the hour is now.

sentences.zh: 群司百辟，僉諧厥議。

translations.literal: All officials and the hundred ranks are of one voice in this deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister and every office agrees as one in this counsel.

sentences.zh: 但成周歔脊，弗堪胥宇。

translations.literal: But the people of Cheng-Zhou groan and cannot bear to dwell together.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the folk of Cheng-Zhou groan and cannot bear to share one roof.

sentences.zh: 今可於伊雒營建東京，便即設官分職，以為民極也。

translations.literal: Now we may build the Eastern Capital on the Yi and Luo, and at once establish offices and divide duties, to be the people's pole.
translations.idiomatic: Now we may raise the Eastern Capital on the Yi and Luo, and forthwith set offices and divide duties, to be the people's anchor.

sentences.zh: 夫宮室之制，本以便生人；

translations.literal: The design of palaces and houses is fundamentally to benefit the living;
translations.idiomatic: Palaces exist fundamentally to serve the living;

sentences.zh: 上棟下宇，足以避風露。

translations.literal: rafters above and walls below are enough to ward off wind and dew.
translations.idiomatic: beams above and walls below suffice to keep off wind and dew.

sentences.zh: 高臺廣廈，豈曰適形？

translations.literal: Are lofty terraces and broad halls said to suit the form?
translations.idiomatic: Are high towers and vast halls called fitting forms?

sentences.zh: 故《傳》云：儉，德之恭；

translations.literal: Thus the Record says: frugality is the respect of virtue;
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: frugality is virtue's reverence;

sentences.zh: 侈，惡之大。

translations.literal: extravagance is the greatest of evils.
translations.idiomatic: extravagance is the greatest evil.

sentences.zh: 宣尼有云：與其不遜也，寧儉。

translations.literal: Confucius said: rather than lack modesty, better frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Better be sparing than be without modesty.

sentences.zh: 豈謂瑤臺瓊室，方為宮殿者乎？

translations.literal: Does this mean jade towers and jeweled chambers alone are palaces?
translations.idiomatic: Does he mean only jade towers and jeweled halls count as palaces?

sentences.zh: 土階采椽，而非帝王者乎？

translations.literal: Earthen steps and unadorned rafters—are these not the marks of an emperor-king?
translations.idiomatic: Earthen steps and plain rafters—are these not an emperor's hallmarks?

sentences.zh: 是知非天下以奉一人，乃一人以主天下也。

translations.literal: From this one knows it is not that all under Heaven serves one man, but that one man holds all under Heaven in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Hence one knows: not that the world serves one man, but that one man holds the world in trust.

sentences.zh: 民惟國本，本固邦寧。

translations.literal: The people are the root of the state; when the root is firm the state is secure.
translations.idiomatic: The people are the state's root; firm the root, secure the state.

sentences.zh: 百姓足，孰與不足。

translations.literal: When the common people have enough, who lacks enough?
translations.idiomatic: When the people are full, who is wanting?

sentences.zh: 今所營構，務從節儉。

translations.literal: What is now to be built must follow economy.
translations.idiomatic: What we build now must follow thrift.

sentences.zh: 無令雕墻峻宇，復起於當今；

translations.literal: Do not let carved walls and towering houses rise again in the present age;
translations.idiomatic: Let no carved wall or towering house rise again in our day;

sentences.zh: 俗使卑宮菲食，將貽於後世。

translations.literal: rather let low palaces and plain food be handed down to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: but let low halls and plain fare be left to posterity.

sentences.zh: 有司明為條格，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: The responsible offices must set clear regulations that accord with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let the responsible offices draw clear rules that match my intent.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙丑，以右武衛將軍來護兒為右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: On the day yichou of the twelfth month, Right Martial Guard General Lai Huer was appointed Right Commander-in-Chief of the Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou of the twelfth month, Right Martial Guard General Lai Huer became Right Valiant Cavalry Commander.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以柱國李景為右武衛大將軍，以右衛率周羅為右武候大將軍。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Pillar of State Li Jing was appointed Right Martial Guard Commander-in-Chief, and Right Guard Colonel Zhou Luohou was appointed Right Martial Guard Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Pillar Li Jing became Right Martial Guard commander, and Right Guard colonel Zhou Luohou became Right Martial Guard commander.

sentences.zh: 大業元年春正月壬辰朔，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the first year of Daye, on the day renchen at the new moon, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, first month, Daye year one, on renchen at the new moon, he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 立妃蕭氏為皇后。

translations.literal: Consort Xiao was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He made Consort Xiao empress.

sentences.zh: 改豫州為溱州，洛州為豫州。

translations.literal: Yu Province was changed to Qin Province, and Luo Province to Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yu became Qin, and Luo became Yu.

sentences.zh: 廢諸州總管府。

translations.literal: All area commander headquarters of prefectures were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: All prefectural area-commander offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 丙申，立晉王昭為皇太子。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, Prince of Jin Zhao was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Prince Zhao of Jin was made crown prince.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以上柱國宇文述為左衛大將軍，上柱國郭衍為左武衛大將軍，延壽公於仲文為右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Supreme Pillar Yuwen Shu was appointed Left Guard Commander-in-Chief, Supreme Pillar Guo Yan Left Martial Guard Commander-in-Chief, and Duke of Yanshou Yu Zhongwen Right Guard Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Supreme Pillar Yuwen Shu became Left Guard commander, Supreme Pillar Guo Yan Left Martial Guard commander, and Duke Yu Zhongwen of Yanshou Right Guard commander.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以豫章王暕為豫州牧。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Prince of Yuzhang Yang was appointed Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Prince Yang of Yuzhang became Governor of Yu.

sentences.zh: 戊申，發八使巡省風俗。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, eight envoys were dispatched to tour and inspect local customs.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, he sent eight commissioners to tour local customs.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：昔者哲王之理天下也，其在愛民乎？

translations.literal: An edict said: In antiquity when the sage kings ordered all under Heaven, was it not in loving the people?
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: When sage kings ordered the world of old, was it not by loving the people?

sentences.zh: 既富而教，家給人足，故能風教淳厚，遠至邇安。

translations.literal: Having enriched them, they taught them; when every household had its fill, customs could be made pure and thick, and peace reached from far to near.
translations.idiomatic: Enrich, then teach; when households had enough, custom grew pure and peace ran from far to near.

sentences.zh: 理定功成，率由斯道。

translations.literal: When order was settled and achievement complete, all followed this path.
translations.idiomatic: When order stood firm and work was done, all followed this road.

sentences.zh: 朕恭嗣寶位，撫育黎獻，夙夜戰兢，若臨川谷。

translations.literal: I reverently succeeded to the precious throne and nurture the black-haired people, trembling day and night as if standing over a ravine.
translations.idiomatic: I reverently took the throne and nurture the people, trembling day and night as over a chasm.

sentences.zh: 雖則聿遵先緒，弗敢失墜，永言政術，多有缺然。

translations.literal: Though I follow the former course and dare not let it fall, speaking always of the art of government, much is still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Though I follow my predecessor's path and dare not let it slip, in the art of rule much still falls short.

sentences.zh: 況以四海之遠，兆民之眾，未獲親臨，問其疾苦。

translations.literal: How much more when the four seas are distant and the hundred thousand myriad people stretch wide—I have not yet gone in person to ask after their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: All the more when the seas are wide and the myriad folk are many—I have not yet gone in person to ask their hardships.

sentences.zh: 每慮幽仄莫舉，冤屈不申，一物失所，用傷和氣。

translations.literal: I always worry that the obscure and lowly are not raised up, that wrongs are not redressed, that when one thing loses its place harmony is harmed.
translations.idiomatic: I fret that the obscure go unchosen, grievances go unheard, and a single loss of place wounds harmony.

sentences.zh: 萬方有罪，責在朕躬，所以興寤增嘆，而夕惕載懷者也。

translations.literal: When all under Heaven has guilt, the blame lies on my person—therefore I rise from sleep with sighs and carry vigilance evening and morning.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm is guilty, the fault is mine—hence I wake sighing and keep vigil day and night.

sentences.zh: 今既布政惟始，宜存寬大。

translations.literal: Now that government is first proclaimed, magnanimity should be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Now that rule begins anew, let mercy be kept.

sentences.zh: 可分遣使人，巡省方俗，宣揚風化，薦拔淹滯，申達幽枉。

translations.literal: Envoys may be sent in separate groups to tour and inspect local customs, spread civilizing influence, recommend the submerged and stalled, and convey the obscure and wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys abroad to tour local custom, spread civilizing teaching, lift the buried talent, and bring hidden wrongs to light.

sentences.zh: 孝悌力田，給以優復。

translations.literal: Those filial, dutiful, and strong in fieldwork shall receive preferential exemption from labor.
translations.idiomatic: The filial, dutiful, and field-strong shall receive favorable exemption from corvée.

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨不能自存者，量加振濟。

translations.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves shall receive measured relief according to need.
translations.idiomatic: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the alone who cannot live shall receive measured relief.

sentences.zh: 義夫節婦，旌表門閭。

translations.literal: Righteous husbands and chaste wives shall have their gates marked with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Men of righteousness and women of chastity shall have their gates honored.

sentences.zh: 高年之老，加其板授，並依別條，賜以粟帛。

translations.literal: The very aged shall receive additional honorary staff appointments, and according to separate regulations be granted grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The very old shall receive honorary staff and, by separate rule, grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 篤疾之徒給侍丁者，雖有侍養之名，曾無赒贍之實，明加檢校，使得存養。

translations.literal: For those with grave illness granted attendant laborers, though the name of support exists, in fact there is no relief—let this be clearly inspected so they may be kept and nourished.
translations.idiomatic: For the gravely ill granted attendant labor, though support is named, relief is not given—inspect clearly so they may be kept alive.

sentences.zh: 若有名行顯著，操履修潔；

translations.literal: If there are outstanding reputation and conduct, pure and cultivated integrity;
translations.idiomatic: If reputation and conduct stand forth, and integrity is cultivated;

sentences.zh: 及學業才能，一藝可取，咸宜訪采，將身入朝。

translations.literal: or learning and talent, or any single art worth taking up—all should be sought out and brought to court in person.
translations.idiomatic: or learning and talent, or any art worth taking—all should be sought and brought to court.

sentences.zh: 所在州縣，以禮發遣。

translations.literal: The prefectures and counties where they are found shall send them off with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures and counties of their residence shall dispatch them with ceremony.

sentences.zh: 其蠹政害人，不便於時者，使還之日，具錄奏聞。

translations.literal: As for corrupt government that harms the people and is inconvenient to the times, on the day of return a full record shall be submitted in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: As for harmful corrupt rule inconvenient to the age, on return let a full memorial be submitted.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以吳州總管宇文弼為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, Area Commander of Wu Province Yuwen Bi was appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Wu commander Yuwen Bi became Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 二月己卯，以尚書左僕射楊素為尚書令。

translations.literal: On the day jimao of the second month, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Yang Su was appointed Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao of month two, Left Vice Director Yang Su became Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三月丁未，詔尚書令楊素、納言楊達、將作大匠宇文愷營建東京，徙豫州郭下居民以實之。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei of the third month, an edict ordered Director Yang Su, Chief Counselor Yang Da, and Master of Works Yuwen Kai to build the Eastern Capital and move residents below the walls of Yu Province to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei of month three, the edict ordered Director Yang Su, Counselor Yang Da, and Master of Works Yuwen Kai to build the Eastern Capital and move Yu Province townsmen to fill it.

sentences.zh: 戊申，詔曰：「聽采輿頌，謀及黎庶，故能審政刑之得失。

translations.literal: On the day wushen an edict said: "By listening to carriage songs and consulting the black-haired people, one can examine the gains and losses of government and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen an edict said, "Hearing carriage songs and consulting the people, one judges the gains and losses of law.

sentences.zh: 是知昧旦思治，欲使幽枉必達，彜倫有章。

translations.literal: From this one knows that thinking of governance before dawn is to make hidden wrongs surely reach expression and constant norms have their chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Hence thinking of rule before dawn is to make hidden wrongs heard and norms clear.

sentences.zh: 而牧宰任稱朝委，茍為僥幸，以求考課，虛立殿最，不存理實。

translations.literal: Yet governors and magistrates, bearing the court's commission, merely seek luck and chance to pass examinations, falsely setting grades of excellence and worst without preserving truth in fact.
translations.idiomatic: Yet governors, bearing court commission, seek luck to pass review, falsely setting grades without truth.

sentences.zh: 綱紀於是不理，冤屈所以莫申。

translations.literal: Discipline thereby went unordered, and wrongs therefore could not be voiced.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline thereby failed, and wrongs went unspoken.

sentences.zh: 關河重阻，無由自達。

translations.literal: Passes and rivers lay in heavy obstruction, and there was no way to reach me oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Passes and rivers blocked the way, and none could reach me.

sentences.zh: 朕故建立東京，躬親存問。

translations.literal: I therefore established the Eastern Capital and go in person to inquire after welfare.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore raised the Eastern Capital and go in person to inquire.

sentences.zh: 今將巡歷淮海，觀省風俗。

translations.literal: Now I shall tour the Huai and sea circuits and observe and inspect local customs.
translations.idiomatic: Now I shall tour Huai and sea and observe local custom.

sentences.zh: 眷求讜言，徒繁詞翰，而鄉校之內，闕爾無聞；

translations.literal: I look for loyal words, yet only verbose documents multiply, while within the village schools nothing is heard;
translations.idiomatic: I seek loyal counsel, yet documents multiply, while village schools fall silent;

sentences.zh: 恇然夕惕，用勞興寢。

translations.literal: fearful evening and morning, I toil in rising and sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: fearful evening and morning, I toil waking and sleeping.

sentences.zh: 其民下有知州縣官人政理苛刻，侵害百姓，背公徇私，不便於民者，聽詣朝堂封奏。

translations.literal: If among the people any know that prefectural or county officials are harsh in governance, injure the people, turn their backs on the public for private gain, or are inconvenient to the people, they may come to the court with sealed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: If the people know any prefect or county officer harsh, injurious, partial, or inconvenient, let them bring sealed memorials to court.

sentences.zh: 庶乎四聰以達，天下無冤。

translations.literal: Thus perhaps the four listeners will be reached and all under Heaven will be without wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Thus perhaps the four listeners will hear, and the realm be without wrong.

sentences.zh: 」又於皂澗營顯仁宮，采海內奇禽異獸草木之類，以實園苑。

translations.literal: " Moreover at Zao Ravine the Xianren Palace was built, and strange birds, beasts, and plants from within the seas were gathered to fill the parks and gardens.
translations.idiomatic: " Moreover at Zao Ravine he built Xianren Palace and gathered strange birds, beasts, and plants from within the seas to fill the gardens.

sentences.zh: 徙天下富商大賈數萬家於東京。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of wealthy merchants and great traders from all under Heaven were moved to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of wealthy merchants from the realm were moved to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，發河南諸郡男女七百萬開通濟渠，自西苑引穀、洛水達於河，自板渚引河通於淮。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, seven million men and women from the commanderies of Henan were drafted to open the Tongji Canal, drawing the Gu and Luo from the Western Park to reach the river, and from Banzhu drawing the river to reach the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, seven million men and women of Henan commanderies were levied to open the Tongji Canal, drawing Gu and Luo from Western Park to the river, and from Banzhu drawing the river to the Huai.

sentences.zh: 庚申，遣黃門侍郎王弘、上儀同於士澄往江南采木，造龍舟、鳳拚、黃龍、赤艦樓船等數萬艘。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, Yellow Gate Attendant Wang Hong and Upper Companion of the First Rank Yu Shicheng were sent to the south to gather timber and build dragon boats, phoenix barges, yellow dragon ships, red warship tower-boats, and tens of thousands of vessels besides.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Attendant Wang Hong and Upper Companion Yu Shicheng were sent south to gather timber and build dragon boats, phoenix barges, yellow dragon ships, red tower-ships, and tens of thousands more.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸亥，大將軍劉仲方擊林邑破之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day guihai, Grand General Liu Zhongfang attacked and defeated Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, month four, on guihai, Grand General Liu Zhongfang attacked and defeated Linyi.

sentences.zh: 五月庚戌，戶部尚書、義豐侯韋沖卒。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu of the fifth month, Minister of Revenue, Marquis of Yifeng Wei Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu of month five, Minister of Revenue, Marquis Wei Chong of Yifeng, died.

sentences.zh: 甲子，熒惑入太微。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, Mars entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Mars entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁酉，制戰亡之家，給復十年。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day dingyou, a statute was made that families of those who died in battle received ten years' exemption.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, month seven, on dingyou, a rule granted ten years' exemption to families of the battle-dead.

sentences.zh: 丙午，滕王綸、衛王集並奪爵徙邊。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, Prince of Teng Lun and Prince of Wei Ji both had their titles stripped and were banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Prince Lun of Teng and Prince Ji of Wei were both stripped of rank and banished.

sentences.zh: 閏七月甲子，以尚書令楊素為太子太師，安德王雄為太子太傅，河間王弘為太子太保。

translations.literal: In the intercalary seventh month, on the day jiazi, Director Yang Su was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Prince of Ande Xiong Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and Prince of Hejian Hong Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In intercalary month seven, on jiazi, Director Yang Su became Heir's Grand Tutor, Prince Xiong of Ande Heir's Grand Mentor, and Prince Hong of Hejian Heir's Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 丙子，詔曰：君民建國，教學為先；

translations.literal: On the day bingzi an edict said: In establishing state and ruling the people, teaching comes first;
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi an edict said: In founding state and ruling people, teaching comes first;

sentences.zh: 移風易俗，必自茲始。

translations.literal: to shift custom and change the vulgar must begin from here.
translations.idiomatic: to shift custom and change the vulgar must begin here.

sentences.zh: 而言絕義乖，多歷年代，進德修業，其道浸微。

translations.literal: Yet speech has broken with meaning over many years, and advancing virtue and cultivating achievement have grown ever fainter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet speech has broken from meaning through many years, and advancing virtue and cultivating achievement have grown faint.

sentences.zh: 漢采坑焚之餘，不絕如線；

translations.literal: After the Han gathered what survived the pits and burning, learning hung by a thread;
translations.idiomatic: After Han gathered what survived pits and burning, learning hung by a thread;

sentences.zh: 晉承板蕩之運，掃地將盡。

translations.literal: the Jin inherited a time of turmoil and swept the ground nearly clean.
translations.idiomatic: Jin inherited turmoil and swept the ground nearly bare.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，軍國多虞；

translations.literal: From that time onward, army and state had many troubles;
translations.idiomatic: From that time, army and state knew many troubles;

sentences.zh: 雖復黌宇時建，示同愛禮；

translations.literal: though schoolhouses were sometimes built, showing the same love of ritual;
translations.idiomatic: though schoolhouses were sometimes built, showing love of ritual;

sentences.zh: 函丈或陳，殆為虛器。

translations.literal: lecture halls were sometimes set out, yet nearly became empty vessels.
translations.idiomatic: lecture halls were sometimes opened, yet nearly became empty vessels.

sentences.zh: 遂使紆青拖紫，非以學優；

translations.literal: Thus crimson sashes and purple robes came not from excellence in learning;
translations.idiomatic: Thus purple sashes came not from learning's excellence;

sentences.zh: 制錦操刀，類多墻面。

translations.literal: making brocade and wielding knives mostly faced blank walls.
translations.idiomatic: making brocade and wielding knives mostly faced blank walls.

sentences.zh: 上陵下替，綱維不立，雅缺道消，實由於此。

translations.literal: Superiors collapsed and inferiors replaced them, the net of norms was not established, elegant learning waned and the Way faded—truly because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Superiors fell and inferiors rose, norms were not set, elegant learning waned—truly from this.

sentences.zh: 朕纂承洪緒，思弘大訓。

translations.literal: I have succeeded to the great succession and think to spread the great instruction.
translations.idiomatic: I have succeeded to the great succession and think to spread great teaching.

sentences.zh: 將欲尊師重道，用闡厥繇；

translations.literal: I wish to honor teachers and weight the Way, to open its course;
translations.idiomatic: I wish to honor teachers and weight the Way, to open its course;

sentences.zh: 講信修睦，敦獎名教。

translations.literal: to speak faith and cultivate harmony, to encourage and reward famed teaching.
translations.idiomatic: to speak faith and cultivate harmony, to encourage famed teaching.

sentences.zh: 方今區宇平壹，文軌攸同，十步之內，必有芳草；

translations.literal: Now the realm is unified, writing and wheels are one, and within ten paces there must be fragrant grass;
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is one, script and wheels alike, and within ten paces fragrant grass must grow;

sentences.zh: 四海之中，豈無孝、秀。

translations.literal: within the four seas, how could there be no filial sons and cultivated talents?
translations.idiomatic: within the four seas, how could there be no filial sons and cultivated talents?

sentences.zh: 諸在家及見入學者，若有篤誌好古，耽典悅禮，學行優敏，堪膺時務，所在采訪，具以名聞。

translations.literal: All whether at home or already entered schools—if any have steadfast will and love antiquity, immerse themselves in classics and delight in ritual, excel in conduct and quickness of mind, and can meet the needs of the age—wherever found, let full names be reported.
translations.idiomatic: All at home or in schools—if any love antiquity steadfastly, immerse in classics, excel in conduct, and can meet the age—wherever found, report their names.

sentences.zh: 即當隨其器能，擢以不次。

translations.literal: At once according to their capacity they shall be promoted out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: At once by their capacity promote them out of turn.

sentences.zh: 若研精經術，未顧進仕，可依其藝業深淺，門廕高卑，雖未升朝，並量準給祿。

translations.literal: If they refine classics and arts and do not yet seek office, according to the depth of their craft and the height or lowness of their family privilege, though not yet risen to court, salary shall be measured and granted alike.
translations.idiomatic: If they refine classics and do not seek office, by depth of craft and family privilege grant salary though not yet at court.

sentences.zh: 庶夫恂恂善誘，不日成器，濟濟盈朝，何遠之有。

translations.literal: Then earnest good guidance will in no long day complete vessels, and the court will brim full—how far can that be?
translations.idiomatic: Then earnest guidance will soon complete vessels, and the court brim full—how far is that?

sentences.zh: 其國子等學，亦宜申明舊制，教習生徒，具為課試之法，以盡砥礪之道。

translations.literal: The National University and like schools should also declare the old regulations, teach and drill students, and fully set methods of examination to exhaust the path of whetstone grinding.
translations.idiomatic: The National University and like schools should declare old rules, teach students, and set examination methods to exhaust grinding on the whetstone.

sentences.zh: 八月壬寅，上御龍舟幸江都，以左武衛大將軍郭衍為前軍，右武衛大將軍李景為後軍。

translations.literal: On the day renyin of the eighth month the Emperor boarded the dragon boat to visit Jiangdu, with Left Martial Guard Commander-in-Chief Guo Yan as vanguard and Right Martial Guard Commander-in-Chief Li Jing as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin of month eight, the Emperor boarded the dragon boat for Jiangdu, Guo Yan of Left Martial Guard as vanguard and Li Jing of Right Martial Guard as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 文武官五品以上給樓船，九品以上給黃篾。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials of fifth rank and above were given tower ships; ninth rank and above were given yellow bamboo rafts.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials of fifth rank and above received tower ships; ninth rank and above yellow bamboo rafts.

sentences.zh: 舳艫相接，二百餘里。

translations.literal: Stern to stern they linked for more than two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Stern to stern they linked for more than two hundred li.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己丑，赦江、淮已南，揚州給復五年；

translations.literal: On the day jichou of the tenth winter month, amnesty was granted south of the Jiang and Huai, and Yang Province received five years' exemption;
translations.idiomatic: On jichou of the tenth winter month, amnesty south of Jiang and Huai, and Yang Province five years' exemption;

sentences.zh: 舊總管內，給復三年。

translations.literal: within the old area commands, three years' exemption.
translations.idiomatic: within the old area commands, three years' exemption.

sentences.zh: 十一月己未，以大將軍崔仲方為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei of the eleventh month, Grand General Cui Zhongfang was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei of month eleven, Grand General Cui Zhongfang became Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月辛酉，東京成，賜監督者有差。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the second year, on the day xinyou, the Eastern Capital was completed and supervisors were rewarded in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, month one, year two, on xinyou, the Eastern Capital was completed and supervisors rewarded in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 以大理卿梁毗為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Liang Pi was appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Court Review Grand Judge Liang Pi became Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，遣十使，並省州縣。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, ten envoys were dispatched to tour and reduce prefectures and counties together.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, ten envoys were sent to tour and reduce prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 二月丙戌，詔尚書令楊素、吏部尚書牛弘、大將軍宇文愷、內史侍郎虞世基、禮部侍郎許善心制定輿服。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu an edict ordered Director Yang Su, Minister of Civil Office Niu Hong, Grand General Yuwen Kai, Palace Secretariat Attendant Yu Shiji, and Vice Minister of Rites Xu Shansin to fix chariots and robes.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, the edict ordered Director Yang Su, Minister Niu Hong, Grand General Yuwen Kai, Attendant Yu Shiji, and Vice Minister Xu Shansin to fix chariots and robes.

sentences.zh: 始備輦輅及五時副車。

translations.literal: For the first time imperial carriages and the five seasonal secondary chariots were readied.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time imperial carriages and the five seasonal secondary chariots were readied.

sentences.zh: 上常服皮弁，十有二琪。

translations.literal: The Emperor's regular dress was the leather cap with twelve jade beads.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's regular dress was the leather cap with twelve jade beads.

sentences.zh: 文官弁服，佩玉；

translations.literal: Civil officials' cap dress with jade pendants;
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials wore cap dress with jade pendants;

sentences.zh: 五品已上，給犢車通憲；

translations.literal: fifth rank and above were given calf carts with barred hubs;
translations.idiomatic: fifth rank and above received calf carts with barred hubs;

sentences.zh: 三公、親王加油絡。

translations.literal: the Three Dukes and imperial princes received oiled net canopies in addition.
translations.idiomatic: the Three Dukes and imperial princes received oiled net canopies besides.

sentences.zh: 武官平巾幘，褲褶；

translations.literal: Military officials wore flat headcloth and trousers with jacket;
translations.idiomatic: Military officials wore flat headcloth and jacket-trousers;

sentences.zh: 三品已上，給瓟槊。

translations.literal: third rank and above were given gourd-handled spears.
translations.idiomatic: third rank and above received gourd-handled spears.

sentences.zh: 下至胥吏，服色各有差。

translations.literal: Down to clerks and attendants, dress colors each had their differences.
translations.idiomatic: Down to clerks and attendants, dress colors differed each from each.

sentences.zh: 非庶人不得戎服。

translations.literal: Commoners might not wear military dress.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners might not wear military dress.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，置都尉官。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Commandant offices were established.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Commandant offices were established.

sentences.zh: 三月庚午，車駕發江都。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu of the third month the imperial carriage departed Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu of month three, the imperial carriage left Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 先是，太府少卿何稠、太府丞雲定興盛修儀仗，於是課州縣送羽毛。

translations.literal: Before this, Vice Minister of the Imperial Storehouse He Chou and Assistant Director Yun Dingxing had lavishly repaired ceremonial regalia, and therefore commanderies and counties were charged to deliver feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Imperial Storehouse Vice Minister He Chou and Assistant Director Yun Dingxing had lavishly repaired ceremonial regalia, and commanderies and counties were charged to deliver feathers.

sentences.zh: 百姓求捕之，網羅被水陸，禽獸有堪氈毦之用者，殆無遺類。

translations.literal: The people sought to catch them; nets spread over water and land, and birds and beasts usable for felt and down were nearly exhausted in kind.
translations.idiomatic: The people sought to catch them; nets spread over water and land, and birds and beasts usable for felt and down were nearly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 至是而成。

translations.literal: By this time it was completed.
translations.idiomatic: By this time it was completed.

sentences.zh: 夏四月庚戌，上自伊闕，陳法駕，備千乘萬騎，入於東京。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day gengxu, the Emperor came from Yique, arrayed the law chariot, with a thousand chariots and ten thousand riders, and entered the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, month four, on gengxu, the Emperor came from Yique, arrayed the law chariot with a thousand chariots and ten thousand riders, and entered the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，上御端門，大赦天下，免今年租賦。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai the Emperor faced the Duan Gate, proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm, and remitted this year's rent and levies.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, the Emperor faced the Duan Gate, proclaimed general amnesty, and remitted this year's rent and levies.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以冀州刺史楊文思為民部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Inspector of Ji Province Yang Wensi was appointed Minister of the People.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Ji Inspector Yang Wensi became Minister of the People.

sentences.zh: 五月甲寅，金紫光祿大夫、兵部尚書李通坐事免。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin of the fifth month, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of War Li Tong was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin of month five, Grand Master Li Tong of Splendid Happiness, Minister of War, was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，詔曰：「旌表先哲，式在饗祀。

translations.literal: On the day yimao an edict said: "To mark and honor former sages is the form of sacrificial feasting.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao an edict said, "To mark and honor former sages is the form of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 所以優禮賢能，顯彰遺愛。

translations.literal: Thus one gives preferential rites to the worthy and able and makes manifest lingering love.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one gives preferential rites to the worthy and makes lingering love manifest.

sentences.zh: 朕永鑒前修，尚想名德，何嘗不興嘆九原，屬懷千載。

translations.literal: I eternally mirror former cultivation and still think on famed virtue—how have I not sighed over the nine plains and cherished the thousand years?
translations.idiomatic: I eternally mirror former cultivation and still think on famed virtue—how have I not sighed over the nine plains and cherished a thousand years?

sentences.zh: 其自古以來賢人君子，有能樹聲立德，佐世匡時，博利殊功，有益於人者，並宜營立祠宇，以時致祭。

translations.literal: All from antiquity onward worthy men and noble gentlemen who could establish reputation and plant virtue, aid the age and correct the times, spread broad merit and special achievement, and benefit people—all should have shrines built and receive seasonal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: All worthy men and noble gentlemen from antiquity who established reputation, aided the age, spread merit, and benefited people should have shrines built and receive seasonal sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 墳壟之處，不得侵踐。

translations.literal: At tombs and mounds there must be no encroachment or treading.
translations.idiomatic: At tombs and mounds there must be no encroachment.

sentences.zh: 有司量為條式，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: The responsible offices shall measure and set regulations that accord with my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Let responsible offices measure and set regulations that accord with my intent.

sentences.zh: 」六月壬子，以尚書令、太子太師楊素為司徒。

translations.literal: " In the sixth month, on the day renzi, Director and Heir's Grand Tutor Yang Su was appointed Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: " In month six, on renzi, Director and Heir's Grand Tutor Yang Su became Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 進封豫章王暕為齊王。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang Yang was advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yang of Yuzhang was advanced to Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸丑，以衛尉卿衛玄為工部尚書。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day guichou, Commandant of the Court of the Imperial Stud Xuan was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, month seven, on guichou, Stud Commandant Xuan became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 庚申，制百官不得計考增級。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, a statute was made that the hundred officials might not advance rank by examination reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, a rule forbade the hundred officials to advance rank by examination reckoning.

sentences.zh: 必有德行功能，灼然顯著者，擢之。

translations.literal: Only if virtue and achievement were clear and outstanding should they be promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Only if virtue and achievement stood clear and outstanding should they be promoted.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，擢籓邸舊臣鮮于羅等二十七人，官爵有差。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, twenty-seven old retainers of the fief including Xianyu Luo were promoted, ranks and titles in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, twenty-seven old fief retainers including Xianyu Luo were promoted, ranks and titles in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，皇太子昭薨。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, Crown Prince Zhao died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Crown Prince Zhao died.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，上柱國、司徒、楚國公楊素薨。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Supreme Pillar, Minister of Education, Duke of Chu Yang Su died.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Supreme Pillar, Minister of Education, Duke Yang Su of Chu, died.

sentences.zh: 八月辛卯，封皇孫倓為燕王，侗為越王，侑為代王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day xinmao, Imperial Grandson Tan was enfeoffed Prince of Yan, Tong Prince of Yue, and You Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In month eight, on xinmao, Grandson Tan was made Prince of Yan, Tong Prince of Yue, and You Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 九月乙丑，立秦王俊子浩為秦王。

translations.literal: On the day yichou of the ninth month, Prince Jun's son Hao of Qin was installed as Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou of month nine, Prince Hao, son of Jun of Qin, was made Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊子，以靈州刺史段文振為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth winter month, on the day wuzi, Inspector of Ling Province Duan Wenzhen was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month, on wuzi, Ling Inspector Duan Wenzhen became Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚寅，詔曰：「前代帝王，因時創業，君民建國，禮尊南面。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin of the twelfth month an edict said: "Former dynasties' emperors, founding enterprises according to the times, established states and ruled the people, with ritual honoring the facing-south throne.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin of month twelve, an edict said, "Former emperors founded states according to the times and ruled the people with ritual facing south.

sentences.zh: 面歷運推移，年代永久，丘壟殘毀，樵牧相趨；

translations.literal: As fortunes shifted and years grew long, mounds and tombs were ruined and woodcutters and herdsmen hurried toward them;
translations.idiomatic: As fortunes shifted and years grew long, mounds were ruined and woodcutters and herdsmen hurried toward them;

sentences.zh: 塋兆堙蕪，封樹莫辨。

translations.literal: burial precincts were choked with weeds and marker trees could not be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: burial precincts were choked with weeds and marker trees could not be told apart.

sentences.zh: 興言淪滅，有愴於懷。

translations.literal: Speaking of their ruin, there was grief in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of their ruin, grief caught the heart.

sentences.zh: 自古以來帝王陵墓，可給隨近十戶，蠲其雜役，以供守視。」

translations.literal: From antiquity onward at imperial tombs, ten nearby households may be granted, exempted from miscellaneous labor, to supply guarding and viewing."
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity at imperial tombs, ten nearby households may be granted, exempted from labor, to guard and watch."

sentences.zh: 三年春正月癸亥，敕并州逆人已流配而逃亡者，所獲之處，即宜斬決。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the third year, on the day guihai, an order said that Bing rebels already banished who fled again should, wherever taken, be beheaded at once.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, month one, year three, on guihai, an order said Bing rebels banished who fled again should be beheaded wherever taken.

sentences.zh: 丙子，長星竟天，出於東壁，二旬而止。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi a long comet filled the sky, appearing from the Eastern Wall and stopping after twenty days.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi a long comet filled the sky from the Eastern Wall and stopped after twenty days.

sentences.zh: 是月，武陽郡上言河水清。

translations.literal: That month Wuyang Commandery reported that the Yellow River was clear.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wuyang Commandery reported the Yellow River clear.

sentences.zh: 二月己丑，慧星見於東井、文昌；

translations.literal: On the day jichou of the second month, a comet appeared at the Well and Literary Glory;
translations.idiomatic: On jichou of month two, a comet appeared at the Well and Literary Glory;

sentences.zh: 歷大陵、五車、北河，入太微，掃帝座，前後百餘日而止。

translations.literal: passing the Great Mound, Five Chariots, and North River, entering the Supreme Enclosure and sweeping the Emperor's Seat, stopping after more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: passing the Great Mound, Five Chariots, and North River, entering the Supreme Enclosure and sweeping the Emperor's Seat, stopping after more than a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 三月辛亥，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai of the third month the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai of month three, the imperial carriage returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以大將軍姚辯為左衛將軍。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, Grand General Yao Bian was appointed Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Grand General Yao Bian became Left Guard General.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，遣羽騎朱寬使於流求國。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Feathered Cavalry Zhu Kuan was sent as envoy to Liuqiu.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Feathered Cavalry Zhu Kuan was sent as envoy to Liuqiu.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，河間王弘薨。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, Prince of Hejian Hong died.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, Prince Hong of Hejian died.

sentences.zh: 夏四月庚辰，詔曰：「古者帝王觀風俗，皆所以憂勤兆庶，安集遐荒。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day gengchen an edict said: "In antiquity emperors observed local customs—all to worry and toil for the myriad people and settle distant wilds.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, month four, on gengchen, an edict said, "In antiquity emperors observed local custom—all to toil for the myriad people and settle distant wilds.

sentences.zh: 自蕃夷內附，未遑親撫，山東經亂，須加存恤。

translations.literal: Since frontier tribes submitted inward, there has been no leisure to comfort them in person; Shandong suffered disorder and needs added care.
translations.idiomatic: Since frontier tribes submitted, there has been no leisure to comfort them; Shandong suffered disorder and needs added care.

sentences.zh: 今欲安輯河北，巡省趙、魏，所司依式。

translations.literal: Now I wish to settle and soothe Hebei and tour Zhao and Wei—the responsible offices shall follow the regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to settle Hebei and tour Zhao and Wei—the responsible offices shall follow regulations."

sentences.zh: 」甲申，頒律令，大赦天下，關內給復三年。

translations.literal: " On the day jiashen, laws and ordinances were promulgated, a general amnesty proclaimed throughout the realm, and the interior passes granted three years' exemption.
translations.idiomatic: " On jiashen, laws were promulgated, general amnesty proclaimed, and the interior passes granted three years' exemption.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，改州為郡。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, provinces were changed to commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, provinces were changed to commanderies.

sentences.zh: 改度量衡，並依古式。

translations.literal: Weights and measures were changed to follow the ancient forms.
translations.idiomatic: Weights and measures were changed to follow ancient forms.

sentences.zh: 改上柱國以下官為大夫。

translations.literal: Officials from Supreme Pillar of State downward were changed to grand masters.
translations.idiomatic: Officials from Supreme Pillar downward were changed to grand masters.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔曰：天下之重，非獨理所安；

translations.literal: On the day jiawu an edict said: The weight of all under Heaven is not settled by governance alone;
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu an edict said: The weight of the realm is not settled by governance alone;

sentences.zh: 帝王之功，豈一士之略。

translations.literal: the achievement of an emperor-king is not the strategy of a single man.
translations.idiomatic: the achievement of an emperor is not the strategy of one man.

sentences.zh: 自古明君哲後，立政經邦，何嘗不選賢與能，振拔淹滯。

translations.literal: From antiquity enlightened rulers and sage successors, establishing government and ordering the state—how have they not chosen the worthy and able and raised the submerged and stalled?
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity enlightened rulers establishing government—how have they not chosen the worthy and raised the submerged?

sentences.zh: 周稱多士，漢號得人，尚想前風，載懷欽佇。

translations.literal: Zhou was called rich in scholars, Han famed for gaining men—I still think on the former wind and cherish reverent longing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was called rich in scholars, Han famed for gaining men—I still think on the former wind with reverent longing.

sentences.zh: 朕負扆夙興，冕旒待旦。

translations.literal: I bear the throne and rise early, the imperial cap waiting for dawn.
translations.idiomatic: I bear the throne and rise early, the imperial cap waiting for dawn.

sentences.zh: 引領巖谷，置以周行；

translations.literal: I stretch toward mountain valleys and place them in the court ranks;
translations.idiomatic: I stretch toward mountain valleys and place men in court ranks;

sentences.zh: 冀與群才，共康庶績。

translations.literal: I hope with all talent jointly to bring peace to the myriad achievements.
translations.idiomatic: I hope with all talent jointly to bring peace to the myriad achievements.

sentences.zh: 而匯茅寂漠，投竿罕至。

translations.literal: Yet the thatched selection lies silent and the fishing pole rarely arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the thatched selection lies silent and the fishing pole rarely arrives.

sentences.zh: 豈美璞韜采，未值良工；

translations.literal: Is it that fine jade hides its luster and has not met the good craftsman;
translations.idiomatic: Is it that fine jade hides its luster and has not met the good craftsman;

sentences.zh: 將介石在懷，確乎難拔？

translations.literal: or that the unyielding stone lies in the breast and is firmly hard to pull?
translations.idiomatic: or that the unyielding stone lies in the breast and is firmly hard to pull?

sentences.zh: 永鑒則哲，憮然興嘆。

translations.literal: Eternally mirroring the wise, I rise sighing.
translations.idiomatic: Eternally mirroring the wise, I rise sighing.

sentences.zh: 凡厥在位，譬諸股肱，若濟巨川，義同舟楫。

translations.literal: All who hold office are like arms and legs; if crossing a great stream, righteousness is sharing the boat and oar.
translations.idiomatic: All who hold office are like arms and legs; crossing a great stream, righteousness is sharing boat and oar.

sentences.zh: 豈得保茲寵祿，晦爾所知，優遊卒歲，甚非謂也。

translations.literal: How can one keep this favor and salary and hide what one knows, roaming idly through the year—this is very far from what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: How can one keep favor and salary and hide what one knows, roaming idly through the year—this is far from what is meant.

sentences.zh: 祁大夫之舉善，良史以為至公；

translations.literal: Qi Daifu's raising the good—the good historian took it as utmost fairness;
translations.idiomatic: Qi Daifu's raising the good—the good historian took it as utmost fairness;

sentences.zh: 臧文仲之蔽賢，尼父譏其竊位。

translations.literal: Zang Wenzhong's hiding the worthy—Confucius mocked him for usurping place.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Wenzhong's hiding the worthy—Confucius mocked him for usurping place.

sentences.zh: 求諸往古，非無褒貶。

translations.literal: Seeking it in former antiquity, praise and blame were not lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking it in antiquity, praise and blame were not lacking.

sentences.zh: 宜思進善，用匡寡薄。

translations.literal: You should think to advance the good and use it to correct my thinness.
translations.idiomatic: You should think to advance the good and correct my thinness.

sentences.zh: 夫孝悌有聞，人倫之本；

translations.literal: Filial piety and brotherly duty heard of are the root of human relations;
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety and brotherly duty heard of are the root of human relations;

sentences.zh: 德行敦厚，立身之基。

translations.literal: thick virtue and conduct are the foundation of establishing the person.
translations.idiomatic: thick virtue and conduct are the foundation of the person.

sentences.zh: 或節義可稱，或操履清潔，所以激貪厲俗，有益風化。

translations.literal: Or if integrity and righteousness may be praised, or conduct and bearing are pure and clean—all to stir greed and sharpen custom and benefit civilizing influence.
translations.idiomatic: Or if integrity may be praised, or conduct is pure—all to stir greed, sharpen custom, and benefit civilizing influence.

sentences.zh: 強毅正直，執憲不撓，學業優敏，文才美秀；

translations.literal: Strong, firm, upright, and straight, holding law without bending; excellent in learning and quick in mind, beautiful in literary talent;
translations.idiomatic: Strong, firm, upright, holding law without bending; excellent in learning, beautiful in literary talent;

sentences.zh: 並為廊廟之用，實乃瑚璉之資。

translations.literal: all are for use in the hall and canopy and truly material for ritual vessels.
translations.idiomatic: all are for hall and canopy use and truly ritual-vessel material.

sentences.zh: 才堪將略，則拔之以禦侮；

translations.literal: If talent suits generalship, then raise them to repel insult;
translations.idiomatic: If talent suits generalship, raise them to repel insult;

sentences.zh: 力有驍壯，則任之以爪牙。

translations.literal: if strength has fierceness and strength, then assign them as claws and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: if strength has fierceness, assign them as claws and teeth.

sentences.zh: 爰及一藝可取，亦宜采錄；

translations.literal: Extending to a single art worth taking, it too should be gathered and recorded;
translations.idiomatic: Extending to a single art worth taking, it too should be recorded;

sentences.zh: 若眾善畢舉，與時無棄。

translations.literal: if all goods are together raised, none in the time will be discarded.
translations.idiomatic: if all goods are together raised, none in the time will be discarded.

sentences.zh: 以此求理，庶幾非遠。

translations.literal: By this to seek order, perhaps it is not far.
translations.idiomatic: By this to seek order, perhaps it is not far.

sentences.zh: 文武有職事者，五品已上，宜依令十科舉人。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials with duties, fifth rank and above, should according to the order recommend men in ten categories.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials with duties, fifth rank and above, should recommend men in ten categories.

sentences.zh: 有一於此，不必求備。

translations.literal: Having one among these, completeness is not required.
translations.idiomatic: Having one among these, completeness is not required.

sentences.zh: 朕當待以不次，隨才升用。

translations.literal: I shall treat them out of turn and promote according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: I shall treat them out of turn and promote according to talent.

sentences.zh: 其見任九品已上官者，不在舉送之限。

translations.literal: Those now holding office of ninth rank and above are not within the limit of recommendation and dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Those now holding office of ninth rank and above are not within the recommendation limit.

sentences.zh: 丙申，車駕北巡狩。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, the imperial carriage toured north on imperial hunt.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, the imperial carriage toured north on imperial hunt.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以刑部尚書宇文弼為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Minister of Punishments Yuwen Bi was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Minister of Punishments Yuwen Bi became Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，敕百司不得踐暴禾稼。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, an order said the hundred offices must not tread down and ravage grain in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, an order said the hundred offices must not tread down grain in the fields.

sentences.zh: 其有須開為路者，有司計地所收，即以近倉酬賜，務從優厚。

translations.literal: Where roads must be opened, the responsible offices shall reckon the harvest of the land taken and compensate from the nearest granary, striving for generous treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Where roads must be opened, responsible offices shall reckon the harvest taken and compensate from the nearest granary generously.

sentences.zh: 己亥，至赤岸澤，以太牢祭故太師李穆。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, arriving at Red Bank Marsh, the greatest victims were offered in sacrifice to the late Grand Mentor Li Mu.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, arriving at Red Bank Marsh, the greatest victims were offered to the late Grand Mentor Li Mu.

sentences.zh: 五月丁巳，突厥啟民可汗遣子拓特勒來朝。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi of the fifth month, Qimin Khan of the Turks sent his son Tuotele to court.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi of month five, Qimin Khan of the Turks sent his son Tuotele to court.

sentences.zh: 戊午，發河北十餘郡丁男，自太行山達於并州，以通馳道。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, laborers from more than ten commanderies of Hebei, from the Taihang Mountains reaching Bing Province, were drafted to open the imperial highway.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, laborers from more than ten Hebei commanderies, from the Taihang Mountains to Bing Province, were drafted to open the imperial highway.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，啟民可汗遣其兄子毗黎伽特勒來朝。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, Qimin Khan sent his elder brother's son Pilijia Tele to court.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Qimin Khan sent his elder brother's son Pilijia Tele to court.

sentences.zh: 辛未，啟民可汗使請自入寒奉迎輿駕，上不許。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Qimin Khan sent asking to enter the cold himself to welcome the imperial carriage—the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Qimin Khan asked to enter the cold himself to welcome the imperial carriage—the Emperor did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，有星孛於文昌，上將星常皆動搖。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, a comet appeared at Literary Glory; the Upper General star and the Constant star all shook.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, a comet appeared at Literary Glory; the Upper General and Constant stars all shook.

sentences.zh: 六月辛巳，獵於連谷。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi of the sixth month, a hunt was held at Liangu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi of month six, a hunt was held at Liangu.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔曰：聿追孝饗，德莫至焉；

translations.literal: On the day dinghai an edict said: Pursuing filial sacrifice—virtue has nothing higher;
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai an edict said: Pursuing filial sacrifice—virtue has nothing higher;

sentences.zh: 崇建寢廟，禮之大者。

translations.literal: raising and building sleeping temples is the greatest of rites.
translations.idiomatic: raising sleeping temples is the greatest of rites.

sentences.zh: 然則質文異代，損益殊時。

translations.literal: Yet substance and pattern differ by age, decrease and increase differ by time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet substance and pattern differ by age, decrease and increase differ by time.

sentences.zh: 學滅坑焚，經典散逸；

translations.literal: Learning was extinguished in pits and burning, classics scattered and lost;
translations.idiomatic: Learning was extinguished in pits and burning, classics scattered;

sentences.zh: 憲章湮墜，廟堂制度，師說不同。

translations.literal: statutes and ordinances sank and fell, and hall and temple systems differed in masters' teachings.
translations.idiomatic: statutes sank, and hall and temple systems differed in masters' teachings.

sentences.zh: 所以世數多少，莫能是正，連室異宮，亦無定準。

translations.literal: Therefore how many generations in succession could not be corrected, and connected chambers and separate palaces also had no fixed standard.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore how many generations could not be corrected, and connected chambers and separate palaces had no fixed standard.

sentences.zh: 朕獲奉祖宗，欽承景業，永惟嚴配，冀隆大典。

translations.literal: I have received and served the ancestors, reverently inheriting the glorious enterprise, ever thinking on solemn matching and hoping to elevate the great canon.
translations.idiomatic: I have served the ancestors, inheriting the glorious enterprise, ever thinking on solemn matching and hoping to elevate the great canon.

sentences.zh: 於是詢謀在位，博訪儒術。

translations.literal: Thereupon counsel was sought from those in office and Confucian arts broadly consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon counsel was sought from those in office and Confucian arts broadly consulted.

sentences.zh: 咸以為高祖文皇帝受天明命，奄有區夏。

translations.literal: All considered that Emperor Wen the Cultured of Gaozu received Heaven's bright mandate and suddenly held the Middle Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: All considered that Emperor Wen the Cultured received Heaven's mandate and held the Middle Kingdom.

sentences.zh: 拯群飛於四海，革雕弊於百王。

translations.literal: He rescued the flocking birds throughout the four seas and changed carved decay among the hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: He rescued the flocking birds throughout the four seas and changed carved decay among the hundred kings.

sentences.zh: 恤獄緩刑，生靈皆遂其性；

translations.literal: He eased prisons and slowed punishments, and living beings all followed their nature;
translations.idiomatic: He eased prisons and slowed punishments, and living beings all followed their nature;

sentences.zh: 輕徭薄賦，比屋各安其業。

translations.literal: he lightened corvée and thin levies, and every household rested secure in its work.
translations.idiomatic: he lightened corvée and thin levies, and every household rested secure in its work.

sentences.zh: 芟夷宇宙，混壹車書。

translations.literal: He mowed the universe and unified chariots and script.
translations.idiomatic: He mowed the universe and unified chariots and script.

sentences.zh: 東漸西被，無思不服；

translations.literal: East soaking and west covering, none thought but submitted;
translations.idiomatic: East soaking and west covering, none but submitted;

sentences.zh: 南征北怨，俱荷來蘇。

translations.literal: south campaigning and north complaining, all bore coming renewal.
translations.idiomatic: south campaigning and north complaining, all bore coming renewal.

sentences.zh: 駕毳乘風，歷代所弗至；

translations.literal: Driving plumed carts on the wind, what no age had reached;
translations.idiomatic: Driving plumed carts on the wind, what no age had reached;

sentences.zh: 辮髪左衽，聲教所罕及。

translations.literal: braided hair and left lapel, what transforming teaching rarely touched.
translations.idiomatic: braided hair and left lapel, what transforming teaching rarely touched.

sentences.zh: 莫不厥角關塞，頓顙闕庭；

translations.literal: None but presented horns at the passes and bowed foreheads at the court;
translations.idiomatic: None but presented horns at the passes and bowed foreheads at the court;

sentences.zh: 譯靡絕時，書無虛月。

translations.literal: interpreters never ceased in season, books never lacked a month.
translations.idiomatic: interpreters never ceased, books never lacked a month.

sentences.zh: 韜戈偃伯，天下晏如；

translations.literal: Spears were sheathed and weapons stilled, and all under Heaven was tranquil;
translations.idiomatic: Spears were sheathed and weapons stilled, and the realm was tranquil;

sentences.zh: 嘉瑞休征，表裏禔福。

translations.literal: auspicious omens and blessed signs, blessing inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: auspicious omens and blessed signs, blessing inside and out.

sentences.zh: 猗歟偉歟，無得而名者也。

translations.literal: Alas, how grand—there is no grasping it by name.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how grand—there is no grasping it by name.

sentences.zh: 朕又聞之，德厚者流光，理辨者禮縟。

translations.literal: I have also heard that thick virtue sheds flowing light, and clear principle makes ritual rich.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that thick virtue sheds flowing light, and clear principle makes ritual rich.

sentences.zh: 是以周之文、武，漢之高、光，其典章特立，謚號斯重。

translations.literal: Thus Zhou's Wen and Wu, Han's Gao and Guang—their statutes and ordinances stood apart and their posthumous titles were weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhou's Wen and Wu, Han's Gao and Guang—their statutes stood apart and posthumous titles were weighty.

sentences.zh: 豈非緣情稱述，即崇顯之義乎。

translations.literal: Is it not following feeling and giving expression, the meaning of exalted display?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not following feeling and giving expression, the meaning of exalted display?

sentences.zh: 高祖文皇帝宜別建廟宇，以彰巍巍之德；

translations.literal: Emperor Wen the Cultured should separately have a temple built to manifest his towering virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen the Cultured should separately have a temple built to manifest his towering virtue;

sentences.zh: 仍遵月祭，用表蒸蒸之懷。

translations.literal: still following monthly sacrifice to express the steaming steaming feeling.
translations.idiomatic: still following monthly sacrifice to express deep steaming feeling.

sentences.zh: 有司以時創造，務合典制。

translations.literal: The responsible offices shall create it in season, striving to match the canon.
translations.idiomatic: Responsible offices shall create it in season, striving to match the canon.

sentences.zh: 又名位既殊，禮亦異等。

translations.literal: Moreover as name and position differ, ritual also has differing grades.
