translations.literal: On the day yimao of the eleventh month, bandit chief Wang Xuba broke Gaoyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao of month eleven, Wang Xuba broke Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊寅，有大流星如斛，墜明月營，破其沖車。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin of the twelfth month, a great meteor like a hu fell in Lu Mingyue's camp and broke his assault chariot.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin of month twelve, a great meteor fell in Lu Mingyue's camp.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔民部尚書樊子蓋發關中兵，討絳郡賊敬盤陁、柴保昌等，經年不能克。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, an edict ordered Minister of the People Fan Zigai to raise Guanzhong troops to attack Jiang Commandery bandits Jing Pantuo, Chai Baochang, and others; for years he could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Fan Zigai attacked Jing Pantuo and Chai Baochang for years without success.

sentences.zh: 譙郡人朱粲擁眾數十萬寇荊、襄，僭稱楚帝，建元昌達。

translations.literal: Qiao Commandery man Zhu Can held several hundred thousand raiding Jing and Xiang, falsely called himself Emperor of Chu, era Flourishing Reach.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can of Qiao held hundreds of thousands, called himself Emperor of Chu.

sentences.zh: 漢南諸郡，多為所陷焉。

translations.literal: Many commanderies south of the Han were seized by him.
translations.idiomatic: Many commanderies south of the Han fell to him.

sentences.zh: 十二年春正月甲午，雁門人翟松柏起兵於靈丘，眾至數萬，轉攻傍縣。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the twelfth year, on the day jiawu, Yanmen man Zhai Songbai raised troops at Lingqiu, masses reaching tens of thousands, and turned to attack neighboring counties.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, month one, year twelve, on jiawu, Zhai Songbai of Yanmen raised tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 二月己未，真臘遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei of the second month, Zhenla sent an envoy presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei of month two, Zhenla sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 甲子夜，有二大鳥似雕，飛入大業殿，止於禦幄，至明而去。

translations.literal: At midnight on jiazi, two great birds like eagles flew into the Hall of Great Accomplishment, halted on the imperial canopy, and at dawn departed.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on jiazi, two great birds flew into the Hall of Great Accomplishment and departed at dawn.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，東海賊盧公暹率眾萬餘，保於蒼山。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Donghai bandit Lu Gongxuan led more than ten thousand and held Cang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Lu Gongxuan of Donghai held Cang Mountain with ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁巳，顯陽門災。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day dingsi, the Xianyang Gate burned.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, month four, on dingsi, Xianyang Gate burned.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，魏刀兒所部將甄翟兒號歷山飛，眾十萬，轉寇太原。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Wei Daoer's subordinate general Zhen Zhai'er called himself Mountain Flying, masses a hundred thousand, turned to raid Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Zhen Zhai'er called himself Mountain Flying and raided Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 將軍潘長文討之，反為所敗，長文死之。

translations.literal: General Pan Changwen attacked but was defeated by them and Changwen died.
translations.idiomatic: General Pan Changwen was defeated and died.

sentences.zh: 五月丙戌朔，日有蝕之，既。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, bingxu, there was a solar eclipse, total.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu at the new moon of month five, total eclipse.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，大流星殞於吳郡，為石。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, a great meteor fell in Wu Commandery and became stone.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, a great meteor fell in Wu and became stone.

sentences.zh: 壬午，上於景華宮征求螢火，得數斛，夜出遊山而放之，光遍巖谷。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, at Jinghua Palace the Emperor sought fireflies, obtaining several hu; at night he toured the mountains releasing them, light filling valleys and peaks.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, at Jinghua Palace he sought fireflies and at night released them, light filling valleys.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬戌，民部尚書、光祿大夫、濟北公樊子蓋卒。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day renxu, Minister of the People, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Duke of Jibei Fan Zigai died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, month seven, on renxu, Minister Fan Zigai of Jibei died.

sentences.zh: 甲子，幸江都宮，以越王侗、光祿大夫段達、太府卿元文都、檢校民部尚書韋津、右武衛將軍皇甫無逸、右司郎盧楚等總留守事。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi, he visited Jiangdu Palace; Prince of Yue Tong, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Duan Da, Imperial Storehouse Director Yuan Wenzong, Reviewing Minister of the People Wei Jin, Right Martial Guard General Huangfu Wuyi, Right Bureau Attendant Lu Chu, and others were left in overall charge.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, he visited Jiangdu; Prince Tong, Duan Da, Yuan Wenzong, Wei Jin, Huangfu Wuyi, and Lu Chu were left in charge.

sentences.zh: 奉信郎崔民象以盜賊充斥，於建國門表諫不宜巡幸。

translations.literal: Trustworthy Attendant Cui Minxiang, because bandits filled the land, memorialized at Jianguo Gate that it was not fitting to tour.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Cui Minxiang memorialized at Jianguo Gate that touring was not fitting.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，先解其頤，乃斬之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angry, first cut off his face, then beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor cut off his face, then beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，馮翊人孫華自號總管，舉兵為盜。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Fufeng man Sun Hua called himself area commander and raised troops as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Sun Hua of Fufeng raised troops.

sentences.zh: 高涼通守洗寶徹舉兵作亂，嶺南溪洞多應之。

translations.literal: Gaoliang Circuit Defender Xi Bao'che raised troops in disorder; many southern streams and caves responded.
translations.idiomatic: Defender Xi Bao'che rebelled; southern caves responded.

sentences.zh: 己巳，熒惑守羽林，月餘乃退。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, Mars guarded the Feathered Forest more than a month then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Mars guarded the Feathered Forest over a month.

sentences.zh: 車駕次汜水，奉信郎王愛仁以盜賊日盛，諫上，請還西京。

translations.literal: When the carriage halted at Sishui, Trustworthy Attendant Wang Airen, because bandits grew daily, remonstrated that the Emperor should return to the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Sishui, Wang Airen remonstrated to return west.

sentences.zh: 上怒，斬之而行。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry, beheaded him and went on.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor beheaded him and went on.

sentences.zh: 八月乙巳，賊帥趙萬海眾數十萬，自恒山寇高陽。

translations.literal: On the day yisi of the eighth month, bandit chief Zhao Wanhai, masses several hundred thousand, from Hengshan raided Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi of month eight, Zhao Wanhai from Hengshan raided Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 壬子，有大流星如鬥，出王良、閣道，聲如壞墻。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, a great meteor like a dou came from Wangliang and the Heavenly Path, sound like a collapsing wall.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, a great meteor came from Wangliang, sound like a collapsing wall.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，大流星如甕，出羽林。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, a great meteor like a jar came from the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, a great meteor like a jar came from the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 九月丁酉，東海人杜伏威、揚州沈覓敵等作亂，眾至數萬，右禦衛將軍陳棱擊破之。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou of the ninth month, Donghai man Du Fuwei and Yangzhou Shen Midiji and others made disorder, masses reaching tens of thousands; Right Imperial Guard General Chen Leng defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou of month nine, Du Fuwei and Shen Midiji made disorder; Chen Leng defeated them.

sentences.zh: 戊午，有二枉矢，出北斗魁，委曲蛇形，註於南斗。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, two crooked arrows came from the Big Dipper's head, winding serpent-shaped, pointing to the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, two crooked arrows came from the Big Dipper toward the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，安定人荔非世雄殺臨涇令，舉兵作亂，自號將軍。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Anding man Li Feishixiong killed the Lingjing magistrate, raised troops, and called himself general.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Li Feishixiong of Anding rebelled and called himself general.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己丑，開府儀同三司、左翊衛大將軍、光祿大夫、許公宇文述薨。

translations.literal: In the tenth winter month, on the day jichou, Palace Attendant of the First Rank with equal ceremony, Left Wing Guard Commander-in-Chief, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Duke of Xu Yuwen Shu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month, on jichou, Yuwen Shu died.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸未，鄱陽賊操天成舉兵反，自號元興王，建元始興，攻陷豫章郡。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei of the twelfth month, Poyang bandit Cao Tiancheng raised troops, called himself Prince of Yuanxing, era Beginning Rise, and seized Yuzhang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei of month twelve, Cao Tiancheng seized Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以右翊衛大將軍來護為開府儀同三司，行左翊衛大將軍。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, Right Wing Guard Commander-in-Chief Lai Hu'er was appointed Palace Attendant of the First Rank, acting Left Wing Guard Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Lai Hu'er became Palace Attendant, acting Left Wing Guard commander.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，鄱陽人林士弘自稱皇帝，國號楚，建元太平。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Poyang man Lin Shihong called himself emperor, state Chu, era Great Peace.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Lin Shihong called himself emperor of Chu, era Great Peace.

sentences.zh: 攻陷九江、廬陵郡。

translations.literal: He seized Jiujiang and Luling commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Jiujiang and Luling.

sentences.zh: 唐公破甄翟兒於西河，虜男女千口。

translations.literal: The Duke of Tang defeated Zhen Zhai'er at Xihe and captured a thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tang defeated Zhen Zhai'er at Xihe and captured a thousand.

sentences.zh: 十三年春正月壬子，齊郡賊杜伏威率眾度淮，攻陷歷陽郡。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the thirteenth year, on the day renzi, Qi Commandery bandit Du Fuwei led masses across the Huai and seized Liyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, month one, year thirteen, on renzi, Du Fuwei seized Liyang.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，勃海賊竇建德設壇於河間之樂壽，自稱長樂王，建元丁丑。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Bohai bandit Dou Jiande set an altar at Lesou in Hejian, called himself Prince of Changle, era Dingchou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Dou Jiande called himself Prince of Changle at Lesou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，賊帥徐圓郎率眾數千破東平郡。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, bandit chief Xu Yuanlang led several thousand and broke Dongping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Xu Yuanlang broke Dongping.

sentences.zh: 弘化人到ＧＣ成聚眾萬餘人為盜，傍郡苦之。

translations.literal: Honghua man Dao Cheng gathered more than ten thousand as bandits; neighboring commanderies suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Honghua man Dao Cheng gathered ten thousand as bandits; neighboring commanderies suffered.

sentences.zh: 二月壬午，朔方人梁師都殺郡丞唐世宗，據郡反，自稱大丞相。

translations.literal: On the day renwu of the second month, Shuofang man Liang Shidu killed the assistant governor Tang Shizong, held the commandery in rebellion, called himself Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu of month two, Liang Shidu killed Tang Shizong and rebelled as Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 遣銀青光祿大夫張世隆擊之，反為所敗。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Zhang Shilong was sent to attack but was defeated by them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shilong was sent but defeated.

sentences.zh: 戊子，賊帥王子英破上谷郡。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, bandit chief Wang Ziying broke Shanggu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Wang Ziying broke Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 己丑，馬邑校尉劉武周殺太守王仁恭，舉兵作亂，北連突厥，自稱定楊可汗。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Mayi Colonel Liu Wuzhou killed Governor Wang Rengong, raised troops, linked north with Turks, and called himself Dingyang Khan.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Liu Wuzhou killed Wang Rengong, linked Turks, and called himself Dingyang Khan.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，賊帥李密、翟讓等陷興洛倉。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, bandit chiefs Li Mi and Zhai Rang and others seized Xingluo Granary.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Li Mi and Zhai Rang seized Xingluo Granary.

sentences.zh: 越王侗遣武賁郎將劉長恭、光祿少卿房崱擊之，反為所敗，死者十五六。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Tong sent Martial Guard Officer Liu Changgong and Vice Grand Master Fang Zha to attack; they were defeated by bandits; fifteen or sixteen in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tong sent Liu Changgong and Fang Zha; fifteen or sixteen in ten died.

sentences.zh: 庚子，李密自號魏公，稱元年；

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Li Mi called himself Duke of Wei, era name year one;
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Li Mi called himself Duke of Wei, era year one;

sentences.zh: 開倉以賑群盜，眾至數十萬。

translations.literal: opened granaries to relieve bandit masses, masses reaching several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: opened granaries to relieve masses, reaching hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 河南諸郡，相繼皆陷焉。

translations.literal: Henan commanderies in succession all fell to them.
translations.idiomatic: Henan commanderies in succession fell.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，劉武周破武賁郎將王智辯於桑幹鎮，智辯死之。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Liu Wuzhou defeated Martial Guard Officer Wang Zhibian at Sanggan Post; Zhibian died.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Liu Wuzhou defeated Wang Zhibian at Sanggan; Zhibian died.

sentences.zh: 三月戊午，廬江人張子路舉兵反，遣右禦衛將軍陳棱討平之。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu of the third month, Lujiang man Zhang Zilu raised troops; Right Imperial Guard General Chen Leng pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu of month three, Zhang Zilu rebelled; Chen Leng pacified them.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，賊帥李通德眾十萬寇廬江，左屯衛將軍張鎮州擊破之。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, bandit chief Li Tongde, masses a hundred thousand, raided Lujiang; Left Garrison Guard General Zhang Zhenzhou defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Li Tongde raided Lujiang; Zhang Zhenzhou defeated them.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸未，金城校尉薛舉率眾反，自稱西秦霸王，建元秦興。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day guiwei, Jincheng Colonel Xue Ju led masses in rebellion, called himself Hegemon of Western Qin, era Qin Rise.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, month four, on guiwei, Xue Ju rebelled as Hegemon of Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 攻陷隴右諸郡。

translations.literal: He seized Longyou commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Longyou commanderies.

sentences.zh: 己丑，賊帥孟讓夜入東都外郭，燒豐都市而去。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, bandit chief Meng Rang entered the outer wall of the Eastern Capital at night, burned Fengdu Market, and left.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Meng Rang burned Fengdu Market at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，李密陷迥洛東倉。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Li Mi seized Huiluo East Granary.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Li Mi seized Huiluo East Granary.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，賊帥房憲伯陷汝陰郡。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, bandit chief Fang Xianbo seized Yiyin Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Fang Xianbo seized Yiyin.

sentences.zh: 是月，光祿大夫武賁郎將裴仁基、淮陽太守趙佗等，並以眾叛歸李密。

translations.literal: That month, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Martial Guard Officer Pei Renji, Huaiyang governor Zhao Tuo, and others all led masses in rebellion to join Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Pei Renji, Zhao Tuo, and others joined Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 五月辛酉夜，有流星如甕，墜於江都，甲子，唐公起義師於太原。

translations.literal: On the night of xinyou of the fifth month, a meteor like a jar fell at Jiangdu; on jiazi, the Duke of Tang raised an army at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou night a meteor fell at Jiangdu; on jiazi the Duke of Tang raised army at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，突厥數千寇太原，唐公擊破之。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, several thousand Turks raided Taiyuan; the Duke of Tang defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Turks raided Taiyuan; the Duke of Tang defeated them.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬子，熒惑守積屍。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day renzi, Mars guarded the Corpse Accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, month seven, on renzi, Mars guarded Corpse Accumulation.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，武威人李軌舉兵反，攻陷河曲諸郡，自稱涼王，建元安樂。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Wuwei man Li Gui raised troops, seized Hexi commanderies, called himself Prince of Liang, era Peace and Joy.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Li Gui of Wuwei rebelled as Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 八月辛巳，唐公破武牙郎將宋老生於霍邑，斬之。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi of the eighth month, the Duke of Tang defeated Martial Guard Officer Song Laosheng at Huoyi and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi of month eight, the Duke of Tang defeated Song Laosheng at Huoyi and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 九月己丑，帝括江都人女、寡婦以配從兵。

translations.literal: On the day jichou of the ninth month, the Emperor conscripted Jiangdu women and widows to assign to followers.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou of month nine, the Emperor conscripted Jiangdu women and widows for followers.

sentences.zh: 是月，武陽郡丞元寶藏以郡叛歸李密，與賊帥李文相攻陷黎陽倉。

translations.literal: That month, Wuyang assistant Yuan Baozang rebelled with the commandery to Li Mi; with bandit chief Li Wenxiang he seized Liyang Granary.
translations.idiomatic: That month, Yuan Baozang of Wuyang rebelled with the commandery to Li Mi and seized Liyang Granary with Li Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 彗星見於營室。

translations.literal: A comet appeared at the Encampment.
translations.idiomatic: A comet appeared at the Encampment.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁亥，太原陽世洛聚眾萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the tenth winter month, on the day dinghai, Taiyuan man Yang Shiluo gathered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month, on dinghai, Yang Shiluo of Taiyuan gathered more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 寇掠城邑。

translations.literal: They raided walled towns.
translations.idiomatic: They raided walled towns.

sentences.zh: 丙申，羅令蕭銑以縣反，鄱陽人董景珍以郡反，迎銑於羅縣，號為梁王，攻陷傍郡。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, Luo magistrate Xiao Xian rebelled with the county; Poyang man Dong Jingzhen rebelled with the commandery, welcomed Xian at Luo County, called him Prince of Liang, and seized neighboring commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Xiao Xian of Luo rebelled with the county; Dong Jingzhen of Poyang rebelled with the commandery, welcomed Xian at Luo, called him Prince of Liang, and seized neighboring commanderies.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，武賁郎將高毗敗濟北郡賊甄寶車於監山。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Martial Guard Officer Gao Pi defeated Jibei Commandery bandit Zhen Baoche at Jian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Officer Gao Pi defeated Zhen Baoche of Jibei at Jian Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十一月丙辰，唐公入京師。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen of the eleventh month, the Duke of Tang entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen of month eleven, the Duke of Tang entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，遙尊帝為太上皇，立代王侑為帝，改元義寧。

translations.literal: The Emperor raised a palace at Danyang, intending to withdraw to the left of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a palace at Danyang, intending to withdraw south.

sentences.zh: 上起宮丹楊，將遜於江左。

translations.literal: Crows and magpies came to nest on the tent canopy; driving them could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Crows nested on the canopy; driving failed.

sentences.zh: 有烏鵲來巢幄帳，驅不能止。

translations.literal: Mars violated the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: Mars violated the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 熒惑犯太微。

translations.literal: A stone floated from the river into the Yangzi; sunlight scattered like flowing blood; the Emperor greatly hated it.
translations.idiomatic: A stone floated into the Yangzi; sunlight like blood; the Emperor hated it.

sentences.zh: 有石自江浮入於楊子，日光四散如流血，上甚惡之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, Right Garrison Guard General Yuwen Huaji, Martial Guard Officer Sima Dekan, Yuan Li, Palace Gate Attendant Pei Qiantong, Works Supervisor Yuwen Zhiqi, Martial Brave Officer Zhao Xingshu, Valiant Hawk Officer Meng Jing, Secretariat Attendant Yuan Min, Seal Officer Li Fu, Ni Fangyu, Thousand Bull Left Li Xiaoben and younger brother Xiaozhi, Straight Supervisors Xu Hongren and Xue Shiliang, Gate Officer Tang Fengyi, Medical Chief Zhang Kai, and others made disorder with valiant fruit, entering and violating the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: In month three, year two, Yuwen Huaji, Sima Dekan, Yuan Li, Pei Qiantong, Yuwen Zhiqi, Zhao Xingshu, Meng Jing, Yuan Min, Li Fu, Ni Fangyu, Li Xiaoben, Xu Hongren, Xue Shiliang, Tang Fengyi, Zhang Kai, and others rebelled with valiant fruit and violated the palace.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，右屯衛將軍宇文化及、武賁郎將司馬德戡、元禮、監門直閣裴虔通、將作少監宇文智及、武勇郎將趙行樞、鷹揚郎將孟景、內史舍人元敏、符璽郎李覆、牛方裕、千牛左右李孝本、弟孝質、直長許弘仁、薛世良、城門郎唐奉義、醫正張愷等，以驍果作亂，入犯宮闈。

translations.literal: The Emperor died in the Warm Room, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor died in the Warm Room at fifty.

sentences.zh: 上崩於溫室，時年五十。

translations.literal: Empress Xiao ordered palace women to take bed mats for a coffin and bury him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiao ordered bed mats for a coffin.

sentences.zh: 蕭後令宮人撤床簀為棺，以埋之。

translations.literal: After Huaji departed, Right Imperial Guard General Chen Leng escorted the coffin to Chengxian Hall and buried him below Wu Gong Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaji left, Chen Leng buried him below Wu Gong Terrace.

sentences.zh: 化及發後，右禦衛將軍陳棱奉梓宮於成象殿，葬吳公臺下。

translations.literal: At the start of encoffining, his appearance was as in life; all marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At encoffining, his appearance was as in life; all marveled.

sentences.zh: 發斂之始，容貌若生，眾咸異之。

translations.literal: After Great Tang pacified Jiangnan, he was reburied at Leitang.
translations.idiomatic: After Tang pacified Jiangnan, he was reburied at Leitang.

sentences.zh: 大唐平江南之後，改葬雷塘。

translations.literal: At first, since he was a frontier prince and second in order for installation, he always feigned feeling and adorned conduct to fish for empty fame, secretly having a plan to seize the succession.
translations.idiomatic: At first, as frontier prince and second for succession, he feigned conduct for empty fame, secretly planning to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，上自以蕃王，次不當立，每矯情飾行，以釣虛名，陰有奪宗之計。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu greatly valued Empress Wenxian, and her nature was jealous of concubines;
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu valued Empress Wenxian, who was jealous of concubines;

sentences.zh: 時高祖雅重文獻皇后，而性忌妾媵；

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong inwardly had many favorites, and thereby lost love.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong had many favorites and lost love.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇內多嬖幸，以此失愛。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong inwardly had many favorites, and thereby lost love.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong had many favorites and lost love.

sentences.zh: 帝後庭有子皆不育之，示無私寵，取媚於後。

translations.literal: Sons in the rear court he did not raise, showing no private favor, to win the empress's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Sons in the rear court he did not raise, to win the empress.

sentences.zh: 大臣用事者，傾心與交。

translations.literal: Great ministers who held power he bent his heart to befriend.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers in power he befriended.

sentences.zh: 中使至第，無貴賤，皆曲承顏色，申以厚禮。

translations.literal: When palace envoys came to his residence, none by rank failed to bend expression and extend thick gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoys received thick gifts regardless of rank.

sentences.zh: 婢仆往來者，無不稱其仁孝。

translations.literal: Servants and maids coming and going all called him benevolent and filial.
translations.idiomatic: Servants all called him benevolent and filial.

sentences.zh: 又常私入宮掖，密謀於文獻後。

translations.literal: He also often secretly entered the inner palace and plotted with Empress Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He often secretly entered the inner palace and plotted with the empress.

sentences.zh: 楊素等因機構扇，遂成廢立。

translations.literal: Yang Su and others by opportunity fanned flames, and deposing and installing was thereby completed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su and others fanned flames, completing deposing and installing.

sentences.zh: 自高祖大漸暨諒暗之中，蒸淫無度。

translations.literal: From Gaozu's grave illness through the mourning concealment, he was unrestrained in excess.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozu's grave illness through mourning, he was unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 山陵始就，即事巡遊。

translations.literal: When the mountain tomb was first completed, he at once toured.
translations.idiomatic: When the tomb was completed, he at once toured.

sentences.zh: 以天下承平日久，士馬全盛。

translations.literal: Considering all under Heaven long peaceful, horses and weapons in full strength.
translations.idiomatic: Considering the realm long peaceful, horses and weapons full.

sentences.zh: 慨然慕秦皇、漢武之事。

translations.literal: He sighed and admired the affairs of Qin Shi Huang and Han Wu Di.
translations.idiomatic: He admired Qin Shi Huang and Han Wu Di.

sentences.zh: 乃盛理宮室，窮極侈靡。

translations.literal: Then he lavishly ordered palaces, reaching utmost extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: He lavishly ordered palaces to utmost extravagance.

sentences.zh: 召募行人，分使絕域。

translations.literal: He recruited travelers and sent them in separate groups to the ends of the earth.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited travelers and sent them to earth's ends.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃至者，厚加禮賜；

translations.literal: When various barbarians arrived, he richly added ritual gifts;
translations.idiomatic: When barbarians arrived, he richly gifted;

sentences.zh: 有不恭命，以兵擊之。

translations.literal: if any were disrespectful to orders, he struck with troops.
translations.idiomatic: if disrespectful, he struck with troops.

sentences.zh: 盛興屯田於玉門、柳城之外。

translations.literal: He greatly raised garrison agriculture beyond Jade Gate and Willow City.
translations.idiomatic: He raised garrison agriculture beyond Jade Gate and Willow City.

sentences.zh: 課天下富室分道市武馬，疋直十餘萬。

translations.literal: He charged wealthy houses under Heaven to market military horses by circuit; each horse worth more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He charged wealthy houses to market military horses at vast prices.

sentences.zh: 富強坐是而凍餒者，十家而九。

translations.literal: Of the rich and strong, nine in ten households thereby froze and starved.
translations.idiomatic: Nine in ten rich households froze and starved.

sentences.zh: 性多詭譎。。

translations.literal: His nature was much deceitful and treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was much deceitful.

sentences.zh: 所幸之處，不欲人知；

translations.literal: Places he favored visiting, he did not wish people to know;
translations.idiomatic: Places he favored, he wished none to know;

sentences.zh: 每幸之所，輒數道置頓。

translations.literal: each place he favored, he set several routes of halts.
translations.idiomatic: each favored place had several halt routes.

sentences.zh: 四海珍羞殊味，水陸必備焉。

translations.literal: Rare delicacies of the four seas, by water and land all were prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Rare delicacies of the four seas were prepared.

sentences.zh: 求市者無遠不至。

translations.literal: Seekers in the markets came from none too far.
translations.idiomatic: Market seekers came from afar.

sentences.zh: 郡縣官人，競為獻食；

translations.literal: Commandery and county officials competed to present food;
translations.idiomatic: Officials competed to present food;

sentences.zh: 豐厚者進擢，疏儉者獲罪。

translations.literal: the generous were promoted; the sparse and sparing were punished.
translations.idiomatic: the generous were promoted; the sparing were punished.

sentences.zh: 奸吏侵漁，內外虛竭；

translations.literal: Wicked clerks encroached and drained; inside and outside were emptied;
translations.idiomatic: Wicked clerks drained inside and outside;

sentences.zh: 頭會箕斂，人不聊生。

translations.literal: head meeting and rake gathering—people had no livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: extortion left people no livelihood.

sentences.zh: 於時，軍國多務，日不暇給。

translations.literal: At that time army and state had many affairs daily without leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Army and state had many affairs without leisure.

sentences.zh: 帝方驕怠，惡聞政事；

translations.literal: The Emperor was arrogant and slack, hating to hear government;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was arrogant, hating government;

sentences.zh: 冤屈不理，奏請罕決。

translations.literal: wrongs were not judged; memorials rarely decided.
translations.idiomatic: wrongs went unjudged; memorials rarely decided.

sentences.zh: 又猜忌臣下，無所專任。

translations.literal: He also suspected ministers, specializing in none.
translations.idiomatic: He suspected ministers, specializing in none.

sentences.zh: 朝臣有不合意者，必構其罪而族滅之。

translations.literal: If a court minister did not please him, he surely framed guilt and exterminated the clan.
translations.idiomatic: If a minister displeased him, he framed guilt and exterminated clan.

sentences.zh: 高颎、賀若弼先皇心膂，參謀帷幄；

translations.literal: Gao Feng and He Ruobi were the former emperor's heart and belly, planning in the tent;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Feng and He Ruobi planned in the tent;

sentences.zh: 張衡、李金才籓邸惟舊，績著經綸。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng and Li Jincai were old retainers of the fief, achievement shown in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng and Li Jincai were old fief retainers.

sentences.zh: 惡其直道，忌其正義；

translations.literal: He hated their straight Way and envied their upright righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: He hated their straight Way;

sentences.zh: 求其無形之罪，加以丹頸之戮。

translations.literal: seeking formless guilt, adding cinnabar-neck execution.
translations.idiomatic: seeking formless guilt, adding execution.

sentences.zh: 其餘事君盡禮，謇謇匪躬；

translations.literal: The rest served the ruler with full ritual, earnest and not self-seeking;
translations.idiomatic: The rest served with full ritual;

sentences.zh: 無辜無罪，橫受夷戮者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: innocent and without guilt, wrongly receiving extermination—none could be counted.
translations.idiomatic: innocents wrongly exterminated cannot be counted.

sentences.zh: 政刑弛紊，賄貨公行，莫敢有言，道路以目。

translations.literal: Government and punishments were lax and tangled, bribes walked openly, none dared speak, and the road was eyes only.
translations.idiomatic: Government lax, bribes open, none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 六軍不息，百役繁興；

translations.literal: The six armies did not rest, a hundred corvées flourished;
translations.idiomatic: Six armies did not rest, corvées flourished;

sentences.zh: 行者不歸，居者失業；

translations.literal: those on march did not return, dwellers lost their trades;
translations.idiomatic: marchers did not return, dwellers lost trades;

sentences.zh: 人饑相食，邑落為墟，上弗之恤也。

translations.literal: people ate one another from hunger, settlements became ruins, and above he did not pity.
translations.idiomatic: people ate one another, settlements ruins, and he did not pity.

sentences.zh: 東西行幸，靡有定居；

translations.literal: Touring east and west, there was no fixed dwelling;
translations.idiomatic: Touring east and west without fixed dwelling;

sentences.zh: 每以供費不給，逆收數年之賦。

translations.literal: whenever supplies were insufficient, he inversely collected several years' levies in advance.
translations.idiomatic: when supplies failed, he collected years of levies in advance.

sentences.zh: 所至，唯與後宮流連耽湎，惟日不足。

translations.literal: Where he arrived, only with the rear palace he lingered in indulgence, each day not enough.
translations.idiomatic: Where he arrived, only with the rear palace he indulged.

sentences.zh: 招迎姥媼，朝夕共肆醜言。

translations.literal: He welcomed old women to speak ugly words morning and evening together.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed old women for ugly talk morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 又引少年，令與宮人穢亂。

translations.literal: He also brought in youths and ordered them with palace women in filthy disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He brought youths to disorder with palace women.

sentences.zh: 不軌不遜，以為娛樂。

translations.literal: Unorthodox and unyielding, he took it as entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: Unorthodox conduct he took as entertainment.

sentences.zh: 區宇之內，盜賊蜂起；

translations.literal: Within the realm bandits swarmed like bees;
translations.idiomatic: Within the realm bandits swarmed;

sentences.zh: 劫掠從官，屠陷城邑。

translations.literal: plundering attendants, slaughtering and falling walled towns.
translations.idiomatic: plundering attendants, slaughtering towns.

sentences.zh: 近臣互相掩蔽，皆隱賊數，不以實對。

translations.literal: Near ministers mutually covered, all hiding bandit numbers, not answering with truth.
translations.idiomatic: Near ministers hid bandit numbers.

sentences.zh: 或有言賊多者，輒大被詰責。

translations.literal: If any spoke of many bandits, he was greatly rebuked and punished.
translations.idiomatic: If any spoke of many bandits, he was rebuked.

sentences.zh: 各求茍免，上下相蒙。

translations.literal: Each sought to escape; above and below deceived one another.
translations.idiomatic: Each sought escape; above and below deceived.

sentences.zh: 每出師徒，敗亡相繼。

translations.literal: Whenever armies went out, defeat and death followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever armies went out, defeat followed.

sentences.zh: 戰士盡力，不加賞賜；

translations.literal: Soldiers gave full strength without added reward;
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers gave full strength without reward;

sentences.zh: 百姓無辜，咸受屠戮。

translations.literal: common people without guilt all received slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: common people without guilt were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 蒸庶積怨，天下土崩；

translations.literal: The masses accumulated resentment; all under Heaven collapsed;
translations.idiomatic: Masses accumulated resentment; the realm collapsed;

sentences.zh: 至於就禽，而猶未之寤也。

translations.literal: when it came to being captured, he still had not awakened.
translations.idiomatic: when captured, he still had not awakened.

sentences.zh: 恭皇帝諱侑，元德太子之子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gong, taboo name You, was the son of the Yuande Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gong, taboo name You, was the Yuande Crown Prince's son.

sentences.zh: 母曰韋妃。

translations.literal: His mother was Consort Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Consort Wei.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，有氣度。

translations.literal: His nature was intelligent and keen, with bearing and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He was intelligent, with bearing and capacity.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，立為陳王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye he was installed as Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year three he was made Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 後數載，徙為代王。

translations.literal: After several years he was moved to Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: After years he became Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝親征遼東，令於京師總留事。

translations.literal: When the Emperor personally campaigned on Liaodong, he was ordered to oversee affairs at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor campaigned on Liaodong, he oversaw the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從幸晉陽，拜太原太守，尋鎮京師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed the court to Jinyang, was appointed Taiyuan governor, and soon guarded the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he followed to Jinyang, became Taiyuan governor, and guarded the capital.

sentences.zh: 義兵入長安，尊煬帝為太上皇，奉帝纂業。

translations.literal: When the righteous army entered Chang'an, the Emperor was honored as Supreme Emperor and Emperor You succeeded to the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army entered Chang'an, Yang was Supreme Emperor and You succeeded.

sentences.zh: 義寧元年十一月壬戌，上即皇帝位於大興殿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Righteous Pacification year one, on the day renxu, the Emperor took the throne at the Hall of Great Accomplishment.
translations.idiomatic: In month eleven, Righteous Pacification year one, on renxu, the Emperor took the throne at the Hall of Great Accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「王道喪亂，天步不康；

translations.literal: An edict said: "The kingly Way is lost in disorder, Heaven's steps are not at peace;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The kingly Way is lost; Heaven's steps are not at peace;

sentences.zh: 屬之於朕，逢此百罹。

translations.literal: entrusted to me, I meet this hundred calamities.
translations.idiomatic: entrusted to me, I meet hundred calamities.

sentences.zh: 繈褓之歲，夙遭憫凶；

translations.literal: In swaddling years I early met pity and loss;
translations.idiomatic: In swaddling years I met loss;

sentences.zh: 孺子之辰，太上播越。

translations.literal: in infant years the Supreme Emperor was cast beyond.
translations.idiomatic: in infant years the Supreme Emperor was cast beyond.

sentences.zh: 興言感動，實疚於懷。

translations.literal: Speaking moves feeling; truly guilt lies in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking moves feeling; guilt lies in the breast.

sentences.zh: 太尉唐公，膺期作宰，糾合義兵，翼戴皇室。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant the Duke of Tang, meeting the age's term, became chief minister, gathered righteous troops, and aided and bore the imperial house.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant the Duke of Tang gathered righteous troops and aided the house.

sentences.zh: 爰奉明詔，弼予幼沖，顯命光臨，天威咫尺。

translations.literal: Then he received the bright edict, assisted my infancy; august mandate approached, Heaven's awesomeness within a foot.
translations.idiomatic: He received the edict, assisted my infancy; Heaven's awesomeness near.

sentences.zh: 對揚尊號，悼心失圖；

translations.literal: Facing the honored title, grieving heart lost design;
translations.idiomatic: Facing the honored title, grieving heart lost design;

sentences.zh: 一人在遠，三讓不遂；

translations.literal: one man far away, three refusals did not succeed;
translations.idiomatic: one man far away, three refusals failed;

sentences.zh: 僶勉南面，厝身無所。

translations.literal: diligently facing south, with no place to set the body.
translations.idiomatic: diligently facing south, no place to set the body.

sentences.zh: 茍利社稷，莫敢或違；

translations.literal: If it profits the altars, none dares oppose;
translations.idiomatic: If it profits altars, none dares oppose;

sentences.zh: 俯從群議，奉遵聖旨。

translations.literal: bowing to the crowd's deliberation, I follow the sacred edict.
translations.idiomatic: bowing to deliberation, I follow the sacred edict.

sentences.zh: 可大赦天下。

translations.literal: A general amnesty may be proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: General amnesty may be proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 改大業十三年為義寧元年。

translations.literal: Change the thirteenth year of Daye to Righteous Pacification year one.
translations.idiomatic: Change Daye year thirteen to Righteous Pacification year one.

sentences.zh: 十一月十六日昧爽以前，大辟罪已下，皆赦除之；

translations.literal: Before dawn on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month, for capital crimes and below, all are pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn on month eleven day sixteen, capital crimes and below are pardoned;

sentences.zh: 常赦所不免者，不在赦限。

translations.literal: those regular amnesty does not reach are outside the amnesty limit.
translations.idiomatic: regular amnesty exceptions stand outside.

sentences.zh: 」甲子，以光祿大夫、大將軍、太尉唐公為假黃鉞、使持節、大都督內外諸軍事、尚書令、大丞相，進封唐王。

translations.literal: " On the day jiazi, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand General, Grand Commandant the Duke of Tang was made acting Yellow Axe, Commissioner with Staff, Area Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without, Director of the Secretariat, Great Chancellor, advanced to Prince of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: " On jiazi, the Duke of Tang became acting Yellow Axe, area commander, Director, Great Chancellor, Prince of Tang.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，詔曰：「朕惟孺子，未出深宮；

translations.literal: On the day bingyin an edict said: "I consider myself an infant, not yet out of the deep palace;
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin an edict said, "I am an infant, not yet out of the deep palace;

sentences.zh: 太上遠巡，追蹤穆滿。

translations.literal: the Supreme Emperor tours afar, tracing Mu Man.
translations.idiomatic: the Supreme Emperor tours afar.

sentences.zh: 時逢多難，委當尊極；

translations.literal: The time meets many hardships; I am entrusted with the honored pole;
translations.idiomatic: The time meets hardships; I am entrusted with the pole;

sentences.zh: 辭不獲免，恭己臨朝。

translations.literal: refusal could not be obtained; I respectfully face court.
translations.idiomatic: refusal failed; I respectfully face court.

sentences.zh: 若涉大川，罔知所濟；

translations.literal: As if crossing a great river, I know not how to cross;
translations.idiomatic: As crossing a great river, I know not how;

sentences.zh: 民之情偽，曾未之聞。

translations.literal: the people's truth and falsehood, I have never heard.
translations.idiomatic: the people's truth I have never heard.

sentences.zh: 賴股肱戮力，上宰賢良；

translations.literal: Relying on arms and legs joining strength, the chief minister worthy and good;
translations.idiomatic: Relying on arms joining, the chief minister worthy;

sentences.zh: 匡佐沖人，輔其不逮。

translations.literal: assisting the young, mending what is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: assisting the young, mending lack.

sentences.zh: 軍國機務，事無大小；

translations.literal: Army and state critical affairs, nothing small or large;
translations.idiomatic: Army and state affairs, nothing small or large;

sentences.zh: 文武設官，位無貴賤；

translations.literal: civil and martial offices set, posts without rank high or low;
translations.idiomatic: civil and martial posts without rank barrier;

sentences.zh: 憲章賞罰，咸歸相府。

translations.literal: statutes, rewards, and punishments all return to the chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: statutes and punishments return to the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 庶績其凝，責成斯屬。

translations.literal: Many achievements should congeal; responsibility settles there.
translations.idiomatic: Many achievements congeal there.

sentences.zh: 」己巳，以唐王子隴西公建成為唐國世子；

translations.literal: " On the day jisi, the Duke of Tang's son Prince of Longxi Jian'cheng was made Heir of Tang;
translations.idiomatic: " On jisi, Jian'cheng was made Heir of Tang;

sentences.zh: 敦煌公為京兆尹，改封秦公；

translations.literal: the Prince of Dunhuang was Capital Intendant, changed to Prince of Qin;
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Dunhuang became Intendant, changed to Prince of Qin;

sentences.zh: 元吉為齊公。

translations.literal: Yuanji was Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 太原置鎮北府。

translations.literal: Taiyuan had the Fortress Pacifying the North established.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan had Fortress Pacifying the North established.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，張掖康老和舉兵反。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Zhangye Kang Laohe raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Kang Laohe of Zhangye rebelled.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸未，薛舉自稱天子，寇扶風，秦公為元帥擊破之。

translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, the army captured Qu Tu Tong at Wen Township.

translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Zhang Shian seized Lujiang.

translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Dugu Wudu of Heyang surrendered to Li Mi.

translations.idiomatic: On bingchen of month three, Yuwen Huaji killed the Supreme Emperor at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 右禦衛將軍獨孤盛死之。

translations.literal: Right Imperial Guard General Dugu Sheng died.
translations.idiomatic: Right Imperial Guard General Dugu Sheng died.

translations.literal: Tang state set chancellor and below according to old forms.

translations.idiomatic: dance eight rows, set bells and music.

translations.idiomatic: hearing in the morning, dying at evening without regret.

translations.idiomatic: Follow former canon and hurry the honored title.

translations.idiomatic: He trod glorious foundation and received fine mandate.

translations.literal: Land broad as the three dynasties, awesomeness shaking the eight cords.
translations.idiomatic: Land broad as three dynasties, awe shaking eight cords.

translations.literal: The Shanyu bowed forehead; Yuechang sent repeated translation.
translations.idiomatic: The Shanyu bowed forehead; Yuechang sent translation.

translations.literal: Red-deficit coins overflowed within the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Red-deficit coins overflowed the capital;

translations.idiomatic: red-rotten grain filled below passes.

translations.literal: Bearing his rich and strong resources, he thought to unleash insatiable desire.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing rich resources, he unleashed insatiable desire.

translations.literal: Narrowing Yin and Zhou's systems, esteeming Qin and Han's models.
translations.idiomatic: He narrowed Yin and Zhou, esteemed Qin and Han.

translations.literal: Trusting talent and praising self, arrogant and fierce, bright virtue was obscured.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting talent, arrogant and fierce, bright virtue obscured.

sentences.zh: 內懷險躁，外示凝簡。

translations.literal: Within he harbored dangerous impatience; outward he showed frozen simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Within dangerous impatience; outward frozen simplicity.

sentences.zh: 盛冠服以塞其奸，除諫官以掩其過。

translations.literal: Lavish cap and robes to block his wickedness; removing remonstrance officials to cover his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Lavish robes to block wickedness; removing remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 淫荒無度，法令滋彰；

translations.literal: Dissolute without measure, laws and orders ever more manifest;
translations.idiomatic: Dissolute without measure, laws ever more manifest;

translations.literal: teaching cut the four bonds, punishments joined the five cruelties.
translations.idiomatic: teaching cut four bonds, punishments joined five cruelties.

sentences.zh: 誅鋤骨肉，屠劓忠良。

translations.literal: He executed flesh and blood and butchered the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: He executed flesh and blood and butchered the loyal.

translations.literal: Those rewarded saw no achievement; those slaughtered heard no crime.
translations.idiomatic: Those rewarded saw no achievement; those slaughtered heard no crime.

sentences.zh: 驕怒之兵屢動，土木之功不息。

translations.literal: Arrogant angry armies moved repeatedly; earth and wood works did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Arrogant armies moved repeatedly; earth and wood did not cease.

sentences.zh: 頻出朔方，三駕遼左。

translations.literal: He frequently went out to Shuofang and thrice drove to Liao left.
translations.idiomatic: He frequently went to Shuofang and thrice drove to Liao.

sentences.zh: 旌旗萬里，征稅百端。

translations.literal: Banners ten thousand li, levies a hundred ends.
translations.idiomatic: Banners ten thousand li, levies a hundred ends.

translations.literal: Wicked clerks encroached; people could not bear the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked clerks encroached; people could not bear mandate.

translations.idiomatic: Then violent levies, harsh law, and weapons supervised—thereafter none could live.

translations.idiomatic: Soon Xuanggan began at Liyang; Xiongnu besieged Yanmen.

translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven abandoned the middle land for Yang and Yue.

translations.literal: Villains rode opportunity; strong and weak overawed each other;
translations.idiomatic: Villains rode opportunity; strong overawed weak;

translations.literal: passes and bridges closed and did not open; the imperial carriage went but did not return.
translations.idiomatic: passes closed; the carriage did not return.

translations.idiomatic: Added to armies and plague—seventeen or eighteen died in gullies.

translations.literal: Thereupon they gathered like quail and thorn, bristling hair and rising.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they gathered like quail, bristling and rising.

translations.idiomatic: Great ones crossed provinces, calling themselves emperor;

translations.idiomatic: small ones raided cities in thousands.

translations.idiomatic: Blood became rivers; dead like hemp;

translations.idiomatic: Vast nine lands became a field for elk;

translations.literal: above and below deceived; none would think on disorder.

translations.idiomatic: He roused mayfly wings, exhausting night's pleasure.

translations.literal: All under Heaven, none not enemy;
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven, none not enemy;

sentences.zh: 既鐘百六之期，躬踐數終之運，謳歌有屬，笙鐘變響。

translations.literal: Having reached the hundred-six's term, personally treading number's end, songs had their lord, pipes and bells changed sound.
translations.idiomatic: Having reached the hundred-six's term, songs had their lord, pipes changed sound.

sentences.zh: 雖欲不遵堯、舜之跡，庸可得乎。

translations.literal: Though wishing not to follow Yao and Shun's traces, how could it be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Though wishing not to follow Yao and Shun, how could it be obtained.
